"""Branch-and-bound alone vs the hybrid (local search first, then branch-and-bound from that plan).

  python -m evaluation.run_hybrid                       # 10 and 20 feeders
  python -m evaluation.run_hybrid --sizes 10 15 20 30 --seeds 3 --time 20

Per instance: B&B alone (greedy start), the hybrid, and optionally CP-SAT as the answer key (small sizes only).
'proven' = the solver finished with a proof of optimality inside its time budget.
Gap = percent more harm than the best plan found by any of the solvers on that instance.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import math
import statistics as st
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path

from evaluation.oracle_cpsat import solve_oracle
from loadshed import Policy
from loadshed.sim import build_problem, load_tiers, make_grid, slot_of_day
from loadshed.solvers import solve_bnb, solve_hybrid

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--policy", default="configs/policy.yaml")
ap.add_argument("--tiers", default="data/processed/scenarios/tiers.json")
ap.add_argument("--sizes", type=int, nargs="+", default=[10, 20])
ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, default=2)
ap.add_argument("--hours", type=int, nargs="+", default=[17])
ap.add_argument("--time", type=float, default=15.0, help="search budget for B&B alone and for the hybrid")
ap.add_argument("--oracle-time", type=float, default=20.0, help="0 skips CP-SAT")
ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=4)
ap.add_argument("--out", default="data/processed/benchmarks/hybrid_vs_bnb.csv")
a = ap.parse_args()

base = Policy.from_yaml(a.policy)
tiers = load_tiers(a.tiers)
rows = []
for n in a.sizes:
    pol = replace(base, system_switch_budget=max(base.system_switch_budget, math.ceil(0.6 * n)))
    for tier, scen in tiers.items():
        for seed in range(a.seeds):
            for hour in a.hours:
                p = build_problem(make_grid(n, seed), pol, scen, slot_of_day(hour), episode_offset=8)
                b = solve_bnb(p, time_limit_s=a.time, relax_downtime_if_infeasible=False)
                h = solve_hybrid(p, time_limit_s=a.time, seed=seed, relax_downtime_if_infeasible=False)
                o = solve_oracle(p, time_limit_s=a.oracle_time, workers=a.workers,
                                 relax_downtime_if_infeasible=False) if a.oracle_time > 0 else None
                rows.append(dict(
                    n=n, tier=tier, seed=seed, hour=hour,
                    bnb_status=b.status, bnb_harm=b.objective, bnb_bound=b.lower_bound, bnb_s=round(b.runtime_s, 2), bnb_nodes=b.nodes,
                    hy_status=h.status, hy_harm=h.objective, hy_bound=h.lower_bound, hy_s=round(h.runtime_s, 2),
                    hy_nodes=h.nodes, hy_ls_harm=h.ls_objective,
                    cpsat_status=None if o is None else o.status, cpsat_harm=None if o is None else o.objective,
                    cpsat_s=None if o is None else round(o.runtime_s, 2)))
                print(f"n={n} {tier} seed={seed}: B&B {b.status} {b.runtime_s:.1f}s | hybrid {h.status} {h.runtime_s:.1f}s", flush=True)

out = Path(a.out)
out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
with open(out, "w", newline="") as fh:
    w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=list(rows[0]))
    w.writeheader()
    w.writerows(rows)

print("\nproven = finished with a proof of optimality; time is the median over instances the solver PROVED")
print(f"{'n':>3} {'tier':<9} {'inst':>4} | {'proven B&B':>10} {'proven hybrid':>13} | {'time B&B':>8} {'time hyb':>8} | "
      f"{'gap B&B %':>9} {'gap LS-start %':>14} {'gap hybrid %':>12}")
for n in a.sizes:
    for tier in tiers:
        r = [x for x in rows if x["n"] == n and x["tier"] == tier]
        pb = [x for x in r if x["bnb_status"] == "OPTIMAL"]
        ph = [x for x in r if x["hy_status"] == "OPTIMAL"]
        gaps = {"b": [], "l": [], "h": []}
        for x in r:
            known = [v for v in (x["bnb_harm"], x["hy_harm"], x["cpsat_harm"], x["hy_ls_harm"]) if v]
            if not known:
                continue
            best = min(known)
            for k, key in (("b", "bnb_harm"), ("l", "hy_ls_harm"), ("h", "hy_harm")):
                if x[key]:
                    gaps[k].append(100 * (x[key] - best) / best)
        m = lambda v: f"{st.median(v):9.1f}" if v else "      n/a"
        t = lambda v: f"{st.median(v):8.1f}" if v else "     n/a"
        print(f"{n:>3} {tier:<9} {len(r):>4} | {len(pb):>7}/{len(r):<2} {len(ph):>10}/{len(r):<2} | "
              f"{t([x['bnb_s'] for x in pb])} {t([x['hy_s'] for x in ph])} | {m(gaps['b'])} {m(gaps['l']):>14} {m(gaps['h']):>12}")
print("\nwrote", out)



================================================
FILE: evaluation/run_ladder_stats.py
================================================
"""Ladder statistics: how often is each rung of the relaxation ladder needed, and how big is each relaxation?

  python -m evaluation.run_ladder_stats                       # all three families, 20 and 50 feeders
  python -m evaluation.run_ladder_stats --families ratio --sizes 20 --seeds 3 --time-limit 12
  python -m evaluation.run_ladder_stats --resume              # continue an interrupted run

Why families instead of just the three data-derived tiers: inside the observed range of shortfalls (3-20% of
demand, up to 32% at the 99.9th percentile) the ladder is expected to stay at rung 0 under our placeholder
policy. That is itself a result, but it says little about the ladder. So we also push on it:

  ratio     shortfall as a share of demand, from 3% up to 90%     (how much shortfall can the tool absorb?)
  override  a fixed 20% shortfall while the operator forces a growing share of the non-critical feeders to
            stay ON for the whole horizon                         (how do operator overrides push the ladder up?)
  tight     the ratio sweep again with a stricter policy: max downtime 6 slots, 2 switches per feeder per shift
                                                                  (how does the ladder react to stricter rules?)

Per instance we record the rung reached, whether every lower-rung "no plan" was PROVEN, and the size of each
relaxation: extra downtime slots (rung 1), Critical kW-slots that need approval (rung 2), coverage fraction and
uncovered kW (rung 3).
The system switching budget is scaled with grid size, max(base, ceil(0.6 n)): an ASSUMPTION.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import math
import random
import statistics as st
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path
from time import perf_counter

from loadshed import Policy, Tier, solve_ladder
from loadshed.sim import build_problem, make_grid, make_scenario, slot_of_day

FIELDS = ["family", "param", "n", "seed", "hour", "rung", "status", "proven", "harm", "total_shortfall_kw",
          "extra_downtime_slots", "critical_pairs", "critical_kw_slots", "coverage", "uncovered_kw", "ladder_s"]
DEFAULT_RATIOS = [0.03, 0.0684, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50, 0.60, 0.70, 0.80, 0.90]
DEFAULT_KEEP = [0.0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9]


def run_instance(pol, family, param, n, seed, hour, ratio, keep_share, time_limit_s):
    p = build_problem(make_grid(n, seed), pol, make_scenario("r", ratio), slot_of_day(hour), episode_offset=8)
    if keep_share > 0:
        rng = random.Random(1000 * seed + n)
        pool = [f.id for f in p.feeders if f.tier != Tier.CRITICAL]
        chosen = rng.sample(pool, round(keep_share * len(pool)))
        p = replace(p, forced_keep=frozenset((i, t) for i in chosen for t in range(pol.horizon_slots)))
    t0 = perf_counter()
    r = solve_ladder(p, time_limit_s=time_limit_s)
    rel = {x.rule: x for x in r.relaxations}
    return dict(
        family=family, param=param, n=n, seed=seed, hour=hour, rung=r.rung, status=r.status, proven=r.proven,
        harm=None if r.objective is None else round(r.objective, 1), total_shortfall_kw=round(sum(p.shortfall_kw), 1),
        extra_downtime_slots=rel["MAX_DOWNTIME"].magnitude if "MAX_DOWNTIME" in rel else 0,
        critical_pairs=len(r.needs_approval), critical_kw_slots=round(rel["CRITICAL_CUT"].magnitude, 1) if "CRITICAL_CUT" in rel else 0,
        coverage=r.coverage_fraction, uncovered_kw=None if r.uncovered_kw is None else round(sum(r.uncovered_kw), 1),
        ladder_s=round(perf_counter() - t0, 2))


def load_rows(path):
    rows = []
    with open(path, newline="") as fh:
        for r in csv.DictReader(fh):
            for k in FIELDS:
                if k not in ("family", "status", "proven"):
                    r[k] = None if r[k] in ("", None) else float(r[k])
            rows.append(r)
    return rows


def summarize(rows):
    def med(v):
        v = [x for x in v if x is not None]
        return f"{st.median(v):7.2f}" if v else "    n/a"

    for fam, label in (("ratio", "shortfall as a share of demand"), ("override", "share of non-critical feeders forced ON (20% shortfall)"),
                       ("tight", "shortfall share, TIGHT policy (max downtime 6, 2 switches per feeder)")):
        fr = [r for r in rows if r["family"] == fam]
        if not fr:
            continue
        print(f"\n=== family '{fam}': {label} ===")
        print("rung 0 = all rules | 1 = downtime relaxed | 2 = Critical needs approval | 3 = ESCALATE")
        print(f"{'n':>4} {'param':>7} {'inst':>4} | {'rung 0':>6} {'rung 1':>6} {'rung 2':>6} {'rung 3':>6} | "
              f"{'extra downtime slots':>20} | {'Critical kW-slots':>17} | {'coverage':>8} | {'proven':>6} | {'s':>5}")
        for n in sorted({int(r["n"]) for r in fr}):
            for param in sorted({r["param"] for r in fr if int(r["n"]) == n}):
                g = [r for r in fr if int(r["n"]) == n and r["param"] == param]
                cnt = [sum(1 for r in g if int(r["rung"]) == k) for k in range(4)]
                pct = lambda c: f"{100 * c / len(g):5.0f}%"
                r1 = [r["extra_downtime_slots"] for r in g if int(r["rung"]) == 1]
                r2 = [r["critical_kw_slots"] for r in g if int(r["rung"]) == 2]
                r3 = [r["coverage"] for r in g if int(r["rung"]) == 3]
                pv = sum(1 for r in g if r["proven"] == "True")
                print(f"{n:>4} {param:>7.4g} {len(g):>4} | {pct(cnt[0]):>6} {pct(cnt[1]):>6} {pct(cnt[2]):>6} {pct(cnt[3]):>6} | "
                      f"{med(r1):>20} | {med(r2):>17} | {med(r3):>8} | {pv:>3}/{len(g):<2} | {st.mean(r['ladder_s'] for r in g):5.1f}")
        for n in sorted({int(r["n"]) for r in fr}):
            first = sorted({r["param"] for r in fr if int(r["n"]) == n and int(r["rung"]) >= 1})
            print(f"  n={n}: first parameter value where any relaxation was needed: {first[0] if first else 'none in this range'}")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--policy", default="configs/policy.yaml")
    ap.add_argument("--families", nargs="+", default=["ratio", "override", "tight"], choices=["ratio", "override", "tight"])
    ap.add_argument("--sizes", type=int, nargs="+", default=[20, 50])
    ap.add_argument("--ratios", type=float, nargs="+", default=DEFAULT_RATIOS)
    ap.add_argument("--keep-shares", type=float, nargs="+", default=DEFAULT_KEEP)
    ap.add_argument("--override-ratio", type=float, default=0.20)
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, default=4)
    ap.add_argument("--hours", type=int, nargs="+", default=[17])
    ap.add_argument("--time-limit", type=float, default=24.0, help="per ladder call (each solve gets a twelfth of it)")
    ap.add_argument("--budget-per-feeder", type=float, default=0.6)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="data/processed/benchmarks/ladder_stats.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--resume", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    base = Policy.from_yaml(a.policy)
    out = Path(a.out)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    done = set()
    if a.resume and out.exists():
        done = {(r["family"], r["param"], int(r["n"]), int(r["seed"]), int(r["hour"])) for r in load_rows(out)}
    new_file = not (a.resume and out.exists())
    jobs = []
    for fam in a.families:
        for n in a.sizes:
            budget = max(base.system_switch_budget, math.ceil(a.budget_per_feeder * n))
            pol = replace(base, system_switch_budget=budget)
            if fam == "tight":
                pol = replace(pol, max_downtime_slots=6, feeder_switch_budget=2)
            params = a.keep_shares if fam == "override" else a.ratios
            for param in params:
                for seed in range(a.seeds):
                    for hour in a.hours:
                        jobs.append((pol, fam, param, n, seed, hour,
                                     a.override_ratio if fam == "override" else param, param if fam == "override" else 0.0))
    with open(out, "w" if new_file else "a", newline="") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=FIELDS)
        if new_file:
            w.writeheader()
        for k, (pol, fam, param, n, seed, hour, ratio, keep) in enumerate(jobs, 1):
            if (fam, float(param), n, seed, hour) in done:
                continue
            row = run_instance(pol, fam, param, n, seed, hour, ratio, keep, a.time_limit)
            w.writerow(row)
            fh.flush()
            print(f"[{k}/{len(jobs)}] {fam} param={param} n={n} seed={seed}: rung {row['rung']} ({row['status']}) "
                  f"{row['ladder_s']}s", flush=True)
    summarize(load_rows(out))
    print("\nwrote", out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()



================================================
FILE: evaluation/run_robustness.py
================================================
"""Robustness and stability experiments with the rolling-horizon loop.

  python -m evaluation.run_robustness                                  # all four experiments (about 25 min)
  python -m evaluation.run_robustness --experiments margin failure --n 10 --seeds 3
  python -m evaluation.run_robustness --resume                         # continue an interrupted run

  margin     safety margin x load-estimate error. What does insurance against bad load data cost (extra harm)
             and what does it buy (less unserved shortfall)?
  stability  warm start on/off x scenario tier, with a grid large enough for local search. When NOTHING in the world
             changed since the last cycle, how much does the plan change (plan revision), and how often does the
             committed action differ from what the previous plan predicted (commit surprise)? Unplanned reversals =
             an unpredicted switch that undoes a switch made at most 4 slots earlier.
  override   operator overrides. The same episode with and without them: what do they cost in harm?
             ('keep k' forces the k most-cut feeders to stay ON in the middle of the episode; 'cut k' forces k
             otherwise-idle feeders to be cut.)
  failure    breaker failure probability: unserved shortfall, extra switching, how the ladder copes.
  feedback   meter feedback instead of a big margin: a thin 5% margin plus learning each feeder's real load from its
             meter, against no feedback with a thin and with a fat margin, at the same load-estimate error.

Each episode is a full rolling-horizon run: replan every slot, commit one slot, simulate the actuation.
Harm is what was actually suffered (cut harm + switch cost). Unserved = shortfall not covered by REAL relief.
One CSV row per episode is written as soon as it finishes.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import statistics as st
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path
from time import perf_counter

from loadshed import Policy
from loadshed.loop import EpisodeConfig, Override, run_episode
from loadshed.sim import load_tiers, make_grid, make_scenario

FIELDS = ["experiment", "param1", "param2", "n", "seed", "harm", "unserved", "overshoot", "switches", "failed",
          "replans", "relaxed_cycles", "escalations", "quiet_cycles", "plan_revision_quiet", "surprise_quiet",
          "surprises", "unplanned_reversals", "mean_solve_s", "wall_s"]


def build_cfg(policy, n, seed, ratio, margin=None, episode_slots=16, time_limit_s=12.0, **kw):
    pol = policy if margin is None else replace(policy, safety_margin=margin)
    return EpisodeConfig(grid=make_grid(n, seed), policy=pol, scenario=make_scenario("r", ratio, episode_slots=episode_slots),
                         time_limit_s=time_limit_s, seed=seed, **kw)


def episode_row(experiment, p1, p2, n, seed, cfg):
    t0 = perf_counter()
    res = run_episode(cfg)
    m = res.metrics
    return res, dict(
        experiment=experiment, param1=p1, param2=p2, n=n, seed=seed, harm=round(m.total_harm, 1),
        unserved=round(m.unserved_kw_slots, 1), overshoot=round(m.overshoot_kw_slots, 1), switches=m.n_switches,
        failed=m.failed_commands, replans=m.replans, relaxed_cycles=sum(v for k, v in m.rung_counts.items() if k >= 1),
        escalations=m.escalations, quiet_cycles=m.quiet_cycles, plan_revision_quiet=m.plan_revision_rate_quiet,
        surprise_quiet=m.commit_surprise_rate_quiet, surprises=m.commit_surprises,
        unplanned_reversals=m.unplanned_reversals, mean_solve_s=round(m.mean_solve_s, 2), wall_s=round(perf_counter() - t0, 1))


def most_cut_feeders(res, k):
    """The k feeders that were cut for the most slots in an executed episode (ties: feeder order)."""
    ranked = sorted(res.executed.items(), key=lambda kv: -sum(kv[1]))
    return [fid for fid, row in ranked[:k] if sum(row) > 0]


def idle_feeders(res, grid, k):
    """k feeders that were never cut and are not Critical (candidates for a forced cut)."""
    from loadshed import Tier
    crit = {s.id for s in grid.specs if s.tier == Tier.CRITICAL}
    return [fid for fid, row in res.executed.items() if sum(row) == 0 and fid not in crit][:k]


def jobs(a, pol):
    """Yield (experiment, param1, param2, n, seed, config_factory). Overrides need a baseline, so they run lazily."""
    for exp in a.experiments:
        if exp == "margin":
            for sd in a.load_errors:
                for margin in a.margins:
                    for seed in range(a.seeds):
                        yield exp, sd, margin, a.n, seed, lambda sd=sd, margin=margin, seed=seed: build_cfg(
                            pol, a.n, seed, a.ratio, margin, a.episode_slots, a.time_limit, load_error=(sd, 0.0))
        elif exp == "stability":
            tiers = load_tiers(a.tiers)
            for tier, scen in tiers.items():
                for warm in (True, False):
                    for seed in range(a.seeds):
                        yield exp, tier, warm, a.stability_n, seed, lambda scen=scen, warm=warm, seed=seed: build_cfg(
                            pol, a.stability_n, seed, scen.peak_ratio, None, a.episode_slots, a.time_limit, warm_start=warm)
        elif exp == "feedback":
            variants = [("no feedback, margin 5%", 0.05, None), ("no feedback, margin 30%", 0.30, None),
                        ("feedback (alpha 0.7, exact meter), margin 5%", 0.05, (0.7, 0.0)),
                        ("feedback (alpha 0.3, meter noise 10%), margin 5%", 0.05, (0.3, 0.10))]
            for sd in a.load_errors:
                for label, margin, fb in variants:
                    for seed in range(a.seeds):
                        yield exp, sd, label, a.n, seed, lambda sd=sd, margin=margin, fb=fb, seed=seed: build_cfg(
                            pol, a.n, seed, a.ratio, margin, a.episode_slots, a.time_limit, load_error=(sd, 0.0), load_feedback=fb)
        elif exp == "failure":
            for pf in a.failure_probs:
                for seed in range(a.seeds):
                    yield exp, pf, 0, a.n, seed, lambda pf=pf, seed=seed: build_cfg(
                        pol, a.n, seed, a.ratio, None, a.episode_slots, a.time_limit, failure_prob=pf)
        elif exp == "override":
            for seed in range(a.seeds):
                yield exp, "none", 0, a.n, seed, lambda seed=seed: build_cfg(pol, a.n, seed, a.ratio, None, a.episode_slots, a.time_limit)
                for mode, k in [("keep", 1), ("keep", 2), ("keep", 3), ("cut", 1), ("cut", 2)]:
                    yield exp, mode, k, a.n, seed, "OVERRIDE"


def load_rows(path):
    rows = []
    with open(path, newline="") as fh:
        for r in csv.DictReader(fh):
            for k in FIELDS:
                if k not in ("experiment", "param1", "param2"):
                    r[k] = None if r[k] in ("", None) else float(r[k])
            rows.append(r)
    return rows


def summarize(rows):
    def med(v, f="{:8.1f}"):
        v = [x for x in v if x is not None]
        return f.format(st.median(v)) if v else "     n/a"

    def mean(v, f="{:8.1f}"):
        v = [x for x in v if x is not None]
        return f.format(st.mean(v)) if v else "     n/a"

    pct = lambda v: med([None if x is None else 100 * x for x in v], "{:6.1f}%")
    ex = lambda name: [r for r in rows if r["experiment"] == name]

    if ex("margin"):
        print("\n=== margin: safety margin vs load-estimate error (harm actually suffered, and shortfall left unserved) ===")
        print(f"{'load error':>10} {'margin':>7} {'eps':>3} | {'median harm':>11} {'harm vs 5%':>10} | {'mean unserved kW-slots':>22} | {'episodes with any unserved':>26}")
        for sd in sorted({r["param1"] for r in ex("margin")}):
            ref = [r["harm"] for r in ex("margin") if r["param1"] == sd and abs(float(r["param2"]) - 0.05) < 1e-9]
            base = st.median(ref) if ref else None
            for mg in sorted({float(r["param2"]) for r in ex("margin") if r["param1"] == sd}):
                g = [r for r in ex("margin") if r["param1"] == sd and abs(float(r["param2"]) - mg) < 1e-9]
                rel = "     n/a" if not base else f"{100 * (st.median([r['harm'] for r in g]) - base) / base:+9.0f}%"
                print(f"{float(sd):>10.0%} {mg:>7.0%} {len(g):>3} | {med([r['harm'] for r in g], '{:11.0f}')} {rel:>10} | "
                      f"{mean([r['unserved'] for r in g], '{:22.0f}')} | {sum(1 for r in g if r['unserved'] > 0):>20}/{len(g)}")

    if ex("stability"):
        print("\n=== stability: warm start on/off, nothing-changed ('quiet') cycles only ===")
        print(f"{'tier':>9} {'warm':>5} {'eps':>3} | {'plan revision':>13} {'commit surprise':>15} | {'unplanned reversals':>19} | {'switches':>8} | {'harm':>8}")
        for tier in ("mild", "moderate", "crisis"):
            for warm in ("True", "False"):
                g = [r for r in ex("stability") if r["param1"] == tier and r["param2"] == warm]
                if g:
                    print(f"{tier:>9} {warm:>5} {len(g):>3} | {pct([r['plan_revision_quiet'] for r in g]):>13} "
                          f"{pct([r['surprise_quiet'] for r in g]):>15} | {mean([r['unplanned_reversals'] for r in g], '{:19.1f}')} | "
                          f"{mean([r['switches'] for r in g], '{:8.1f}')} | {med([r['harm'] for r in g], '{:8.0f}')}")

    if ex("override"):
        print("\n=== override: the same episode with and without operator overrides ===")
        print("(k is capped by how many feeders the baseline actually cut or left idle; harm ratio = harm with / harm without)")
        print(f"{'override':>10} {'eps':>3} | {'median extra harm':>17} {'median harm ratio':>17} | {'mean unserved kW-slots':>22}")
        base = {int(r["seed"]): r for r in ex("override") if r["param1"] == "none"}
        for mode, k in [("keep", 1), ("keep", 2), ("keep", 3), ("cut", 1), ("cut", 2)]:
            g = [r for r in ex("override") if r["param1"] == mode and int(float(r["param2"])) == k and int(r["seed"]) in base]
            if g:
                extra = [r["harm"] - base[int(r["seed"])]["harm"] for r in g]
                ratio = [r["harm"] / base[int(r["seed"])]["harm"] for r in g if base[int(r["seed"])]["harm"] > 0]
                print(f"{mode + ' ' + str(k):>10} {len(g):>3} | {med(extra, '{:17.0f}')} {med(ratio, '{:16.1f}x')} | {mean([r['unserved'] for r in g], '{:22.0f}')}")

    if ex("feedback"):
        print("\n=== feedback: learning real loads from meters instead of insuring with a big margin ===")
        print(f"{'load error':>10} {'variant':<50} {'eps':>3} | {'median harm':>11} | {'mean unserved kW-slots':>22} | {'episodes with any unserved':>26}")
        for sd in sorted({r["param1"] for r in ex("feedback")}):
            for label in dict.fromkeys(r["param2"] for r in ex("feedback") if r["param1"] == sd):
                g = [r for r in ex("feedback") if r["param1"] == sd and r["param2"] == label]
                print(f"{float(sd):>10.0%} {label:<50} {len(g):>3} | {med([r['harm'] for r in g], '{:11.0f}')} | "
                      f"{mean([r['unserved'] for r in g], '{:22.0f}')} | {sum(1 for r in g if r['unserved'] > 0):>20}/{len(g)}")

    if ex("failure"):
        print("\n=== failure: breaker failure probability ===")
        print(f"{'fail prob':>9} {'eps':>3} | {'failed cmds':>11} {'extra switches':>14} | {'median harm':>11} {'mean unserved kW-slots':>23} | {'relaxed cycles':>14} {'escalations':>11}")
        sw0 = st.mean([r["switches"] for r in ex("failure") if float(r["param1"]) == 0.0] or [0])
        for pf in sorted({float(r["param1"]) for r in ex("failure")}):
            g = [r for r in ex("failure") if float(r["param1"]) == pf]
            print(f"{pf:>9.0%} {len(g):>3} | {mean([r['failed'] for r in g], '{:11.1f}')} {st.mean([r['switches'] for r in g]) - sw0:>14.1f} | "
                  f"{med([r['harm'] for r in g], '{:11.0f}')} {mean([r['unserved'] for r in g], '{:23.0f}')} | "
                  f"{mean([r['relaxed_cycles'] for r in g], '{:14.1f}')} {mean([r['escalations'] for r in g], '{:11.1f}')}")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--policy", default="configs/policy.yaml")
    ap.add_argument("--tiers", default="data/processed/scenarios/tiers.json")
    ap.add_argument("--experiments", nargs="+", default=["margin", "stability", "override", "failure", "feedback"],
                    choices=["margin", "stability", "override", "failure", "feedback"])
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=10, help="grid size for margin, override and failure (10 = exact solver)")
    ap.add_argument("--stability-n", type=int, default=20, help="grid size for stability (above 12 = local search)")
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, default=3)
    ap.add_argument("--ratio", type=float, default=0.20)
    ap.add_argument("--margins", type=float, nargs="+", default=[0.0, 0.05, 0.15, 0.30, 0.50])
    ap.add_argument("--load-errors", type=float, nargs="+", default=[0.1, 0.2, 0.3])
    ap.add_argument("--failure-probs", type=float, nargs="+", default=[0.0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30])
    ap.add_argument("--episode-slots", type=int, default=16)
    ap.add_argument("--time-limit", type=float, default=12.0, help="per replan (each solve gets a twelfth of it)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="data/processed/benchmarks/robustness.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--resume", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    pol = Policy.from_yaml(a.policy)
    out = Path(a.out)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    done = set()
    if a.resume and out.exists():
        done = {(r["experiment"], str(r["param1"]), str(r["param2"]), int(r["n"]), int(r["seed"])) for r in load_rows(out)}
    new_file = not (a.resume and out.exists())
    baselines = {}
    with open(out, "w" if new_file else "a", newline="") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=FIELDS)
        if new_file:
            w.writeheader()
        for exp, p1, p2, n, seed, make in jobs(a, pol):
            if (exp, str(p1), str(p2), n, seed) in done:
                continue
            if make == "OVERRIDE":
                if seed not in baselines:                      # e.g. after --resume: rebuild the baseline (not written again)
                    bcfg = build_cfg(pol, n, seed, a.ratio, None, a.episode_slots, a.time_limit)
                    baselines[seed] = (run_episode(bcfg), bcfg)
                base_res, base_cfg = baselines[seed]
                if p1 == "keep":
                    ids = most_cut_feeders(base_res, p2)
                    ev = tuple(Override(4, 12, i, "keep") for i in ids)
                else:
                    ids = idle_feeders(base_res, base_cfg.grid, p2)
                    ev = tuple(Override(4, 8, i, "cut") for i in ids)
                cfg = replace(base_cfg, events=ev)
            else:
                cfg = make()
            res, row = episode_row(exp, p1, p2, n, seed, cfg)
            if exp == "override" and p1 == "none":
                baselines[seed] = (res, cfg)
            w.writerow(row)
            fh.flush()
            print(f"{exp} {p1} {p2} n={n} seed={seed}: harm {row['harm']}, unserved {row['unserved']}, {row['wall_s']}s", flush=True)
    summarize(load_rows(out))
    print("\nwrote", out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()



================================================
FILE: evaluation/run_scale.py
================================================
"""Scale sweep: every solver across grid sizes and shortfall tiers. OFFLINE benchmark (uses the CP-SAT oracle).

  python -m evaluation.run_scale                                   # 10, 50, 200, 500 feeders, 2 seeds, 17:00
  python -m evaluation.run_scale --sizes 10 50 --seeds 3 --hours 10 17 --ls-time 15
  python -m evaluation.run_scale --resume                          # continue an interrupted run

What is measured per instance
  setup   time to build every feeder's valid patterns (shared by branch-and-bound and local search)
  greedy  both baselines (plain, sticky); local search (ls); branch-and-bound (bnb); CP-SAT oracle (cpsat)
  Time limits apply to the SEARCH of each solver; setup is reported separately.
  Branch-and-bound runs a full search up to --bnb-full-max-n feeders; above that it only computes its root
  lower bound (one node), because there its tree search cannot finish and the bound is what is useful.
  CP-SAT runs up to --oracle-max-n feeders (it gets slow to build and to solve at 500).

Gap = how much MORE harm a plan has than a reference, in percent.
  vs best known = reference is the best plan any solver found (the true gap is at least this)
  vs bound      = reference is the best proven lower bound   (the true gap is at most this)

The system switching budget is scaled with grid size, max(base, ceil(budget_per_feeder * n)): an ASSUMPTION.
One CSV row is written as soon as an instance finishes, so a long run can be stopped and resumed.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import math
import statistics as st
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path
from time import perf_counter

from evaluation.oracle_cpsat import solve_oracle
from loadshed import Policy, verify
from loadshed.metrics import compute_metrics
from loadshed.sim import build_problem, load_tiers, make_grid, slot_of_day
from loadshed.solvers import solve_bnb, solve_greedy, solve_min_conflicts
from loadshed.solvers.patterns import build_patterns

FIELDS = ["n", "tier", "ratio", "seed", "hour", "budget", "setup_s",
          "greedy_ok", "greedy_harm", "greedy_s", "sticky_ok", "sticky_harm", "sticky_s", "best_greedy_harm",
          "ls_status", "ls_harm", "ls_s", "ls_iters",
          "bnb_mode", "bnb_status", "bnb_harm", "bnb_bound", "bnb_nodes", "bnb_s",
          "cpsat_status", "cpsat_harm", "cpsat_bound", "cpsat_s"]


def parse():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--policy", default="configs/policy.yaml")
    ap.add_argument("--tiers", default="data/processed/scenarios/tiers.json")
    ap.add_argument("--sizes", type=int, nargs="+", default=[10, 50, 200, 500])
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, default=2)
    ap.add_argument("--hours", type=int, nargs="+", default=[17])
    ap.add_argument("--ls-time", type=float, default=30.0)
    ap.add_argument("--bnb-time", type=float, default=60.0)
    ap.add_argument("--bnb-full-max-n", type=int, default=50)
    ap.add_argument("--oracle-time", type=float, default=60.0)
    ap.add_argument("--oracle-max-n", type=int, default=200, help="0 disables the oracle")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=8)
    ap.add_argument("--budget-per-feeder", type=float, default=0.6)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="data/processed/benchmarks/scale_sweep.csv")
    ap.add_argument("--resume", action="store_true")
    return ap.parse_args()


def run_instance(a, base, tier, scen, n, seed, hour):
    budget = max(base.system_switch_budget, math.ceil(a.budget_per_feeder * n))
    pol = replace(base, system_switch_budget=budget)
    p = build_problem(make_grid(n, seed), pol, scen, slot_of_day(hour), episode_offset=8)
    row = dict(n=n, tier=tier, ratio=round(scen.peak_ratio, 4), seed=seed, hour=hour, budget=budget)

    t = perf_counter(); g = solve_greedy(p); row["greedy_s"] = round(perf_counter() - t, 3)
    gv = verify(p, g.schedule); gh = compute_metrics(p, g.schedule).total_harm
    t = perf_counter(); s = solve_greedy(p, sticky=True); row["sticky_s"] = round(perf_counter() - t, 3)
    sv = verify(p, s.schedule); sh = compute_metrics(p, s.schedule).total_harm
    ok = lambda v: v.ok and not v.soft
    row.update(greedy_ok=ok(gv), greedy_harm=round(gh, 2), sticky_ok=ok(sv), sticky_harm=round(sh, 2))
    valid = [(h, sc) for h, sc, v in ((gh, g.schedule, gv), (sh, s.schedule, sv)) if ok(v)]
    row["best_greedy_harm"] = round(min(valid, key=lambda x: x[0])[0], 2) if valid else None
    hint = min(valid, key=lambda x: x[0])[1] if valid else None

    t = perf_counter(); pats = build_patterns(p, True); row["setup_s"] = round(perf_counter() - t, 2)

    ls = solve_min_conflicts(p, time_limit_s=a.ls_time, seed=seed, patterns=pats)
    row.update(ls_status=ls.status, ls_harm=None if ls.objective is None else round(ls.objective, 2),
               ls_s=round(ls.runtime_s, 2), ls_iters=ls.iterations)

    if n <= a.bnb_full_max_n:
        b = solve_bnb(p, time_limit_s=a.bnb_time, patterns=pats)
    else:
        b = solve_bnb(p, time_limit_s=a.bnb_time, node_limit=1, patterns=pats)      # root lower bound only
    row.update(bnb_mode=b.mode, bnb_status=b.status, bnb_harm=None if b.objective is None else round(b.objective, 2),
               bnb_bound=None if b.lower_bound is None else round(b.lower_bound, 2), bnb_nodes=b.nodes,
               bnb_s=round(b.runtime_s, 2))

    if 0 < n <= a.oracle_max_n:
        t = perf_counter()
        o = solve_oracle(p, time_limit_s=a.oracle_time, workers=a.workers, hint=hint)
        row.update(cpsat_status=o.status, cpsat_harm=None if o.objective is None else round(o.objective, 2),
                   cpsat_bound=None if o.best_bound is None else round(o.best_bound, 2),
                   cpsat_s=round(perf_counter() - t, 2))
    return row


def load_rows(path):
    num = lambda v: None if v in ("", None) else float(v)
    rows = []
    with open(path, newline="") as fh:
        for r in csv.DictReader(fh):
            rows.append({k: (num(v) if k not in ("tier", "ls_status", "bnb_mode", "bnb_status", "cpsat_status",
                                                  "greedy_ok", "sticky_ok") else v) for k, v in r.items()})
    return rows


def summarize(rows, sizes, tiers):
    def med(v):
        v = [x for x in v if x is not None]
        return f"{st.median(v):7.1f}" if v else "    n/a"

    def secs(v):
        v = [x for x in v if x is not None]
        return f"{st.median(v):6.1f}" if v else "   n/a"

    print("\n=== TIME (median seconds) ===")
    print(f"{'n':>4} {'tier':<9} {'inst':>4} | {'setup':>6} {'greedy':>6} {'sticky':>6} | {'LS':>6} | {'B&B':>6} | {'CP-SAT':>6}")
    for n in sizes:
        for tier in tiers:
            r = [x for x in rows if int(x["n"]) == n and x["tier"] == tier]
            if r:
                print(f"{n:>4} {tier:<9} {len(r):>4} | {secs([x['setup_s'] for x in r])} {secs([x['greedy_s'] for x in r])} "
                      f"{secs([x['sticky_s'] for x in r])} | {secs([x['ls_s'] for x in r])} | "
                      f"{secs([x['bnb_s'] for x in r])} | {secs([x['cpsat_s'] for x in r])}")

    print("\n=== QUALITY: gap in %, median (vs best known plan .. vs best proven lower bound) ===")
    print("  The true gap of a solver lies between its two numbers. 'window' = how well ANYONE can bound the optimum:")
    print("  (best known - best bound) / best bound. A big window means the sizes where nobody can say how far a plan is.")
    print(f"{'n':>4} {'tier':<9} | {'best greedy':>17} | {'local search':>17} | {'B&B (full)':>17} | {'CP-SAT':>17} | {'window':>7} | proven (B&B/CP-SAT)")
    for n in sizes:
        for tier in tiers:
            r = [x for x in rows if int(x["n"]) == n and x["tier"] == tier]
            if not r:
                continue
            cols = {k: ([], []) for k in ("best_greedy", "ls", "bnb", "cpsat")}
            win = []
            for x in r:
                hs = {"best_greedy": x["best_greedy_harm"], "ls": x["ls_harm"], "bnb": x["bnb_harm"], "cpsat": x["cpsat_harm"]}
                ubs = [v for v in hs.values() if v]
                lbs = [v for v in (x["bnb_bound"], x["cpsat_bound"]) if v]
                if not ubs or not lbs:
                    continue
                ub, lb = min(ubs), max(lbs)
                win.append(100 * (ub - lb) / lb)
                for k, h in hs.items():
                    if h:
                        cols[k][0].append(100 * (h - ub) / ub)
                        cols[k][1].append(100 * (h - lb) / lb)
            fmt = lambda k: f"{med(cols[k][0])} ..{med(cols[k][1])}"
            pb = sum(1 for x in r if x["bnb_status"] == "OPTIMAL"); pc = sum(1 for x in r if x["cpsat_status"] == "OPTIMAL")
            print(f"{n:>4} {tier:<9} | {fmt('best_greedy'):>17} | {fmt('ls'):>17} | {fmt('bnb'):>17} | {fmt('cpsat'):>17} | "
                  f"{med(win)} | {pb}/{len(r)}  {pc}/{len(r)}")
    print("\n(B&B above --bnb-full-max-n feeders is a ONE-node run: its harm is the starting greedy plan, only its bound is meaningful.)")


def main():
    a = parse()
    base = Policy.from_yaml(a.policy)
    tiers = load_tiers(a.tiers)
    out = Path(a.out)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    done = set()
    if a.resume and out.exists():
        done = {(int(r["n"]), r["tier"], int(r["seed"]), int(r["hour"])) for r in load_rows(out)}
    new_file = not (a.resume and out.exists())
    with open(out, "w" if new_file else "a", newline="") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=FIELDS, extrasaction="ignore")
        if new_file:
            w.writeheader()
        total = len(a.sizes) * len(tiers) * a.seeds * len(a.hours)
        k = 0
        for n in a.sizes:
            for tier, scen in tiers.items():
                for seed in range(a.seeds):
                    for hour in a.hours:
                        k += 1
                        if (n, tier, seed, hour) in done:
                            continue
                        t0 = perf_counter()
                        row = run_instance(a, base, tier, scen, n, seed, hour)
                        w.writerow(row)
                        fh.flush()
                        print(f"[{k}/{total}] n={n} {tier} seed={seed} hour={hour}: setup {row['setup_s']}s, "
                              f"LS {row['ls_harm']} , total {perf_counter() - t0:.0f}s", flush=True)
    summarize(load_rows(out), a.sizes, list(tiers))
    print("\nwrote", out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Intelligent Load-Shedding Scheduler for Power Grids

# Executive Brief

When a power grid cannot meet demand, utilities cut power to some areas on purpose. This is called **load shedding**. It happens during heatwaves (air conditioners running), festival-season demand spikes, or equipment failure. The goal is to avoid a total blackout. In most of India today this is done reactively and by hand: an operator picks which feeders to cut, often under time pressure, with no clear method to balance safety, disruption, and practicality.

We build in that gap. We do not build a forecaster that predicts a shortfall. We build a **decision-support tool for the control-room dispatcher**: given a shortfall and a list of feeders (with loads and priority levels), it recommends which feeders to cut, in what order, and for how long. We treat this as a **weighted constraint optimization problem**. The tool also checks that the plan can actually be carried out by field staff (limited switching, minimum cut and restore times).

The tool is built to be understood, not trusted blindly:

- Every recommendation comes with a plain reason.
- An independent checker verifies every plan before it is shown.
- The human operator can always override any decision.
- Shedding is treated as the **last resort**, after cheaper options such as buying power or asking interruptible industry to cut.

An optional layer can turn the solver's reasons into plain-language text. It never makes decisions.

The project uses search, constraint solving, optimization, and (optionally) generative AI.

---

# 1. Problem Statement

## 1.1 Who this is for

- **Primary user: the dispatcher.** This is the control-room engineer (discom or SLDC) who decides how much load to shed, which feeders to cut, and for how long, and then issues the instruction. The tool helps this person make a more precise instruction, faster.
- **Secondary user: the field operator (substation operator or lineman).** This person receives the instruction and flips the switch. In this project, the field operator receives a clear printable table. Their real limits (few switch operations per shift, manual breakers) are built into the model so that plans are executable.
- **Later, only if results justify it:** automate the field operator's task. This is a stretch goal, and a human confirmation step stays in place.

## 1.2 Scope

- **S is an input, not an output.** The shortfall is a value the scheduler receives. It may come from a human operator's estimate (for example, "reduce 40 MW now") or, later, from a forecasting module (Section 10). The scheduler is never responsible for predicting it.
- **S is a vector.** S(t) gives the required relief for each time slot in the horizon. The scheduler receives a new S(t) at each replan.
- **Shedding is the residual.** Before shedding, the dispatcher has other options: buying power, backing down generation, asking interruptible industry to cut, voluntary demand response. The tool takes the shortfall that remains after those options. It shows the operator the amount of other relief it assumed.
- **What this is:** scheduled, rotational load shedding at hour scale (15-minute slots).
- **What this is not:** under-frequency load shedding (which acts in seconds), and it does not model network limits (line flows, voltages). Both are out of scope.

## 1.3 The model

**Time.** Slots t = 1..H (for example, 15 minutes each). We plan the whole horizon but commit only the first k slots, then replan.

**Feeders.** Each feeder f has:

- a **priority tier**:
  - **Flexible (F):** shed first. Example: interruptible industry.
  - **Normal (N):** standard homes and shops.
  - **Critical (C):** hospitals, water pumping, emergency services. Shed **last**, and only with explicit operator approval.
- a **feeder type**: urban, rural, agricultural, industrial, or mixed (a mixed feeder carries a critical consumer and is tagged with its highest tier)
- consumer count n_f
- estimated load L_f(t) in each slot (cutting a feeder relieves its **current load**, not its capacity)
- for agricultural feeders, any **promised supply hours**

**Decision.** x[f,t] = 1 if feeder f is cut in slot t, else 0.

**Hard constraints (must hold in any plan):**

1. **Relief.** Total relief in each slot must cover the shortfall: Î£ L_f(t)Â·x[f,t] â‰¥ S(t) + safety margin + restoration surge (see below).
2. **Minimum cut duration and minimum restore duration.** A feeder cannot flip on and off every slot. This is the anti-thrashing rule.
3. **Switching budget.** A maximum number of breaker operations per feeder and in total per shift.
4. **Operator overrides.** Any feeder the operator forces to cut or to stay on is fixed.
5. **Promised supply hours.** Agricultural feeders keep their promised hours on.
6. **Critical tier.** No Critical feeder is cut without explicit operator approval.

**Soft constraint (can be relaxed in a stated order):**

- **Maximum consecutive downtime** per feeder (for example, no feeder off more than 3 hours in a row).

**Restoration surge.** When a feeder comes back after an outage, its load is higher than before (motors, ACs, and pumps start together). Load in the first slot after restore is L_f(t) Ã— (1 + r_f), where r_f grows with outage length. This is added to the required relief in that slot.

**Uncertain load.** L_f(t) is an estimate. We add a safety margin to S(t) and test what happens when real load differs by 10-20%.

**Objective (what we minimize):**

```
total harm  =  Î£ over feeders and slots  [ tier_weight Ã— time_of_day_weight Ã— consumers Ã— (1 + Î² Ã— (r âˆ’ 1)) ]
             +  Î» Ã— overshoot        (cutting more than needed)
             +  Î¼ Ã— switch operations
```

- r is how many slots in a row the feeder has already been off. Each extra hour of continuous outage hurts more than the previous one (convex harm). This makes cuts rotate across feeders without a fairness rule.
- Tier weights are policy inputs set by the operator. Critical weights are very large. The tool does not decide whose pain counts more.
- Time-of-day weights let a night cut cost more than a noon cut. Exam and irrigation hours can be added.

**What the tool reports (no fairness claim):**

- total harm
- shed energy (kWh)
- cut-hours per feeder (mean and maximum, shown as plain numbers)
- longest outage
- number of switch operations
- overshoot
- thrashing rate
- relaxation magnitude
- optimality gap
- solve time

In plain terms: this is a resource-allocation-under-constraints problem, in the same family as exam scheduling, hospital bed allocation, or airline crew scheduling, but applied to something with immediate public consequences and a failure people experience every summer.

---

# 2. Why It Matters

- **The decision step is often manual.** Forecasting shortfalls is widely studied. Deciding what to cut, in what order, under switching limits is commonly done by hand under time pressure in Indian discoms. (Citations from regulator documents and news reports to be added in Phase 1.)
- **Mistakes under pressure are plausible.** Rotation that repeats on the same areas, and critical feeders cut by error, are reported problems. (To be supported with citations before submission.)
- **A shortfall tool can also say "don't shed."** Because it works on the residual after cheaper options, it can show the operator when buying power or asking industry to cut is the better move.

---

# 3. Existing Approaches and Their Limitations

| **Approach** | **How it's used today** | **Limitation (for our purpose)** |
|---|---|---|
| Manual rotational schedules | Discoms publish fixed cut schedules by area, adjusted by hand in a crisis | Slow to adapt when the shortfall changes; no systematic way to compare options |
| Forecasting systems (regression, ensembles) | Predict demand or shortfall | Stop at prediction; the allocation decision is left to a human |
| Greedy heuristic shedding | Cut the largest non-critical loads first until the shortfall is covered | Simple and fast, but ignores outage length, switching limits, and future slots |
| Commercial DERMS/ADMS platforms | Some advanced distribution systems include optimization | We have not evaluated them; their internal logic is not available to us, so we cannot compare against it |
| Optimal load shedding in power-systems research | Mathematical optimization, usually network-based (power-flow) formulations | Network-focused and mathematically heavy; not built for a readable, operator-facing feeder schedule |
| Constraint-based scheduling (exam timetabling, bed allocation, crew scheduling), constraint hierarchies, weighted CSPs, dynamic CSPs, rolling-horizon (MPC-style) scheduling | Established methods for hard/soft constraints, ordered relaxation, and repeated replanning | General methods. We **use** them. We do not claim to have invented them |

**The gap we address:** an open, readable, feeder-level scheduler for hour-scale rotational shedding that (a) includes real field limits, (b) is checked by an independent verifier, (c) is measured against an exact optimum, and (d) keeps the human in control.

*Note: key references to be added and verified in Phase 1 (for example Dechter, "Constraint Processing"; Borning et al. on constraint hierarchies; Bistarelli et al. on semiring-based and weighted CSPs; literature on optimal load shedding and rolling-horizon control; CERC/SLDC material on the deviation settlement mechanism).*

---

# 4. Our Contribution

We build the decision layer between "we know we're short by X kW" and "here is a safe, executable, explainable plan." We claim the **application, the field-informed model, and the evaluation**. We do not claim novelty of the underlying mechanisms.

**Four deliverables, each independently demo-able:**

1. **Model, simulator, verifier, and metrics.**
   A formal model in code (feeders, tiers, slots, constraints, harm), a synthetic grid generator, a scenario generator grounded in public data, an **independent verifier** that checks every schedule against the hard constraints, and a metrics module. Evaluation exists from day one.

2. **Solver benchmark with optimality gaps and a scale sweep.**
   Three solvers, all written from scratch:
   - a **greedy baseline** (rank feeders by harm per kW of relief, cut down the list, respecting the same rules)
   - **branch-and-bound with bounds propagation** (an exact method; bounds propagation tightens limits on the relief sum and the outage-length rules)
   - **weighted min-conflicts local search** (fast and approximate)

   **CP-SAT (Google OR-Tools) is used only as an "answer key"** to compute the best known solution, so we can say "our solver is within X% of optimal." Our solvers do not use it. A cheap **feasibility check** runs first (is there enough sheddable load to meet S(t) in every slot?). Local search only runs on feasible cases. We test feeder counts 10 â†’ 50 â†’ 200 â†’ 500 and report where each solver starts to struggle.

3. **Relaxation ladder with measured severity.**
   When no plan satisfies everything, the tool relaxes rules in a fixed order and reports what it relaxed and by how much:
   1. relax **maximum consecutive downtime**
   2. cut **Critical** feeders, **only with explicit operator approval**
   3. **ESCALATE**: report the remaining shortfall to the human; do nothing automatically

   Severity is measured as a **magnitude** (for example, how many extra hours beyond the downtime limit), not just on/off.

4. **Rolling-horizon replanning with human control.**
   The scheduler replans on a fixed cadence or when the shortfall changes by more than a threshold. It uses the downtime ledger from earlier cycles, the switching budget, and restoration surge. The **operator can force-cut or force-keep any feeder at any time**, and the tool replans around that and logs it. If a feeder fails to trip, that becomes new input and the tool replans. We measure plan **thrashing** and the **cost of operator overrides** (extra harm caused by forcing a decision).

**Optional (not one of the four):** a plain-language explanation layer.
- The **solver** computes the reason for each cut (which constraints were binding, and the cost of the best alternative). For example: "Feeder 12 was cut because it had the lowest harm per kW and was last cut 6 hours ago."
- An LLM may optionally rewrite those reasons as sentences. It never sees or influences decisions, and it can say nothing that is not in the solver's reason log.
- The project works fully without any LLM.

**What we do not claim:**

- We do not predict shortfalls.
- We do not claim a fairness guarantee (see Section 9).
- We do not claim novelty of relaxation hierarchies, constraint optimization, or rolling-horizon planning.
- We do not build a production SCADA integration. Actuation is a simulation with success and failure states.

---

# 5. System Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD

    OP["OPERATOR CONSOLE<br/>Enter shortfall S(t) and other relief already arranged<br/>Approve, force-cut, force-keep, or stop at any time<br/><b>Human always has final control</b>"]

    GS["GRID STATE<br/>Feeder table: tier, type, consumers, load estimates<br/>Downtime ledger â€¢ switch counts â€¢ promised hours"]

    PL["POLICY FILE<br/>Tier weights â€¢ time-of-day weights<br/>Max downtime â€¢ min cut/restore â€¢ switch budget â€¢ safety margin"]

    CC["CONSTRAINT COMPILER<br/>State + policy + S(t) â†’ optimization problem<br/>Variables = feeder Ã— time-slot, values 0 or 1"]

    FC["FEASIBILITY CHECK<br/>Is there enough sheddable load in every slot?"]

    subgraph SOLVERS["SOLVERS - written from scratch"]
        G["Greedy<br/>baseline"]
        BB["Branch-and-bound<br/>+ bounds propagation"]
        MC["Weighted<br/>min-conflicts"]
    end

    RL["RELAXATION LADDER<br/>1. Relax max downtime<br/>2. Cut Critical feeders, only with approval<br/>3. ESCALATE with remaining shortfall"]

    CAND["CANDIDATE SCHEDULE<br/>Feeder â€¢ slot â€¢ action â€¢ reason code"]

    VER["INDEPENDENT VERIFIER<br/>Small, simple checker<br/>Rejects any plan that breaks a hard rule"]

    ACT["ACTUATION (SIMULATED)<br/>Issue cut/restore<br/>Confirm success or flag failure"]

    EV["EVALUATION<br/>Harm â€¢ gap to optimum â€¢ thrashing<br/>Relaxation magnitude â€¢ override cost"]

    OR["CP-SAT ORACLE<br/>Offline only, used for scoring<br/>Never in the decision path"]

    EXP["EXPLAINER (optional)<br/>Reason codes from the solver<br/>Optional LLM rewrites text, read-only"]

    OP --> CC
    GS --> CC
    PL --> CC
    CC --> FC
    FC --> SOLVERS
    SOLVERS --> RL
    RL --> CAND
    CAND --> VER
    VER --> OP
    OP --> ACT
    ACT --> GS
    CAND --> EV
    OR -.-> EV
    CAND --> EXP
```

**Control loop, stated plainly.** The system does not run once. It replans every 5-15 simulated minutes, or whenever the shortfall changes by more than a threshold. Each replan reads the downtime ledger, so a feeder just cut is not casually cut again. Every plan passes the independent verifier before the operator sees it. The operator can approve, change, or override it. Actuation results (including failures) feed back into the grid state.

**Why the verifier matters.** The solvers are treated as untrusted. A small, simple checker validates every schedule. This is what makes it safe to use fast heuristic solvers.

## Agent framing (PEAS)

- **Performance measure:** minimize weighted harm subject to the hard constraints; minimize relaxation when relaxation is needed.
- **Environment:** the grid's current state, the shortfall vector S(t), feeder history, field limits.
- **Actuators:** recommended cut/restore instructions to the dispatcher (executed by simulated field operators).
- **Sensors:** shortfall magnitude, feeder states and load estimates, elapsed downtime per feeder, actuation confirmations.

---

# 6. Data and Simulation Plan

Real feeder-level cut and restore histories are not available in the selected public sources. We use public data to ground demand and shortfall assumptions. Feeder topology, priorities, downtime histories, and shedding decisions are synthetic.

## Primary dataset: Indian state electricity demand (2014-2024)

- **Source:** Hunt and Bloomfield, *Daily electricity demand data for Indian states (2014-2024)*, Zenodo. License: CC BY 4.0. Cite the dataset and keep attribution.
- **Files to download from the record's Files section:**
  - `corrected_peak_unmet_MW.csv` to calibrate shortfall **size and frequency**
  - `corrected_peak_met_MW.csv` to cross-check peak supply
  - `corrected_daily_energy_met_MU.csv` for daily energy context
- These are **daily, state-level** data. They cannot give the shape of S(t) within a day, and they are not feeder-level.

## Intra-day shape (a known gap)

The Zenodo data cannot tell us how a shortfall rises and falls through a day. Check whether Grid-India daily reports or the National Power Portal export give hourly or 15-minute demand. If not, we use a **documented synthetic evening-peak profile** and say so clearly.

## Feeder realism

- Consumer mix and consumers-per-feeder: from a state regulator tariff order or discom documents.
- Load profiles by class (residential, commercial, industrial, agricultural, essential): synthetic and documented.
- Field constraints (switching limits, supply-hour commitments, reliability standards): collected from public sources into `docs/field-constraints.md`. Each entry records its source, and is marked "to be validated by an operator interview when access is possible."

## Official validation and optional context

- **CEA Power Supply Position (Peak):** download one monthly report and cross-check selected state figures against Zenodo.
- **National Power Portal, Demand Met dashboard:** optional. Use only after checking columns, units, time resolution, and geographic coverage.
- **CEA Load Generation Balance Reports:** supplementary planning context only.

## Simulation method

1. Store original CSVs in `data/raw/zenodo_indian_state_demand/`. Do not edit raw files.
2. Inspect columns, dates, units, missing values, and the distribution of zero and non-zero unmet demand.
3. Define **mild, moderate, and crisis** shortfall scenarios from observed values using documented percentiles. Scale them to the synthetic grid's total load rather than assigning state-level MW values directly to a 10-500 feeder model. Convert units explicitly (1 MW = 1,000 kW).
4. Generate synthetic feeder loads, types, tiers, downtime histories, and changing shortfall inputs. At each replan the scheduler receives the current S(t). It does not forecast it.
5. Add realism tests: load-estimate error (Â±10-20%), restoration surge, and actuation failures.

Do not list a Kaggle compilation or hourly state-demand dataset as a confirmed input unless a specific accessible file has been downloaded, inspected, and its license and provenance recorded. Keep `data-sources.md` limited to sources actually verified, including download date, filename, relevant fields, units, resolution, license, and purpose.

---

# 7. Implementation Plan and Timeline

Team of three: **Person A** leads solver implementation, **Person B** leads model, simulation, and replanning, **Person C** leads literature, data, and evaluation. Cross-support is noted where a phase needs more than one person. Each phase has a named owner and a checkable exit criterion.

**Build order principle:** build a thin end-to-end slice first (model, verifier, metrics, greedy, oracle), then add the harder solvers. Evaluation is built from the start, not at the end.

| Phase | Owner | Deliverable | Exit criteria |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Problem formalization, literature, data selection | C (with A, B) | Formal model write-up; related-work table with real citations; `docs/field-constraints.md` from public sources | Formal spec approved by all 3; `data-sources.md` lists â‰¥4 verified, accessible sources; every citation checked |
| 2. Model, verifier, metrics in code | B (A supports) | Data classes (feeder, tier, slot, schedule), `verify(schedule)`, metrics module | Verifier passes hand-made valid cases and rejects hand-made invalid cases for every hard constraint |
| 3. Grid simulation and data pipeline | B, C | Synthetic grid generator; shortfall scenario generator | Valid tagged grids at 10/50/200/500 feeders; scenarios validated against Phase 1 data ranges |
| 4. Thin slice: greedy baseline + CP-SAT oracle | A | Greedy solver; CP-SAT oracle; first optimality gap | Gap computed on 10 and 50 feeder grids; every greedy output passes the verifier |
| 5. Branch-and-bound with bounds propagation | A | Exact solver with feasibility check | Matches the oracle's optimum on all small grids (â‰¤50 feeders); solve times logged |
| 6. Weighted min-conflicts and solver comparison | A, C | Local search solver; comparison table | Table of solve time, harm, and optimality gap across 10/50/200 feeders for all solvers; verifier passes on all outputs |
| 7. Relaxation ladder and ESCALATE | B | Ladder implemented and logged | Ladder fires only when infeasible; order verified; Critical feeders never cut without approval in any test; ESCALATE reports the remaining shortfall; every step logged with magnitude |
| 8. Rolling-horizon loop with field limits and operator control | B (A supports) | Replan loop with ledger, switching budget, restoration surge, force-cut/force-keep, actuation-failure feedback | Replans correctly on cadence and on shortfall change; passes a scripted multi-cycle test; override and failure cases handled and logged |
| 9. Evaluation harness | C (A, B support) | Scale sweep, thrashing test, load-error test, override-cost test, relaxation severity report | Sweep run 10 â†’ 500 feeders; thrashing, relaxation severity, and override cost reported per scenario tier |
| 10. Optional: explainer | A or B | Solver-side reason codes; optional LLM rewrite | Every explanation traces to a logged reason; boundary test shows the LLM cannot produce statements outside the log |
| 11. Report, buffer, demo | All | Full write-up, repo, presentation | Report covers all 4 deliverables with data from Phases 4-9; repo runs clean from a fresh clone; each member can defend any section in the viva |

---

# 8. Evaluation Methodology

- **Correctness.** Every schedule is checked by the independent verifier against all hard constraints. Report a 100% pass rate as a sanity check, not a headline result.
- **Solution quality.** Compare harm across solvers on identical scenarios, and report the **optimality gap** against the CP-SAT oracle.
- **Scalability.** Runtime and gap as feeder count grows (10 â†’ 50 â†’ 200 â†’ 500). Identify where branch-and-bound stops being practical and where local search stays useful. Reaching this limit is a finding, not a failure.
- **Relaxation ladder.** For each scenario tier (mild, moderate, crisis): how often each rung fires, and the magnitude (for example, hours beyond the downtime limit, kW of Critical load cut, residual shortfall at ESCALATE).
- **Replanning stability.** Count feeder on/off flips between consecutive replans with no real change in shortfall or ledger (thrashing). Report a rate per scenario tier and check whether it clusters at planning-window boundaries.
- **Robustness to bad data.** Re-run scenarios with Â±10-20% load error. Report how often the plan fails to cover the real shortfall, and how the safety margin changes that.
- **Cost of operator override.** Force cuts or keeps and measure the extra harm and the extra switching needed.
- **Harm-weight sensitivity (optional).** Run the same scenarios with different tier or feeder weights (for example, a loss-weighted policy that cuts high-loss feeders more) and show how schedules change. The point is to show the effect of a policy choice. We do not claim to know which choice is right.
- **Explanation quality (if built).** Check a sample of explanations against the solver's reason log.

---

# 9. Risks and Honest Limitations

- **Synthetic data risk.** Results are only as credible as the synthetic grid. Mitigation: ground parameters in public documents and state all assumptions.
- **No access to field staff.** Field constraints come from public sources. Mitigation: record every constraint with its source in `docs/field-constraints.md`, and flag each as "needs validation."
- **Solver scalability wall.** Exact solving will likely become impractical well before 500 feeders. This is expected and reported.
- **No fairness guarantee.** We removed fairness constraints and fairness metrics. Fairness is hard to define and measure, and the harm of an outage differs by place and person. The convex outage-length cost makes cuts rotate within an episode, but **we do not guarantee equal treatment over days or weeks**, and we do not claim to. The operator sets the weights; the tool does not decide whose outage matters more.
- **Plan thrashing.** Rolling-horizon replanning can flip a feeder on and off between cycles. Minimum cut and restore durations are built into the model, and thrashing is measured directly.
- **Rough load data.** Real feeder readings can be late or wrong. We use a safety margin and test against error.
- **Restoration surge.** Restoring a feeder adds load. Ignoring it makes the plan wrong in the slot after a restore. It is modeled, but surge values are assumptions.
- **Tool recommending shedding when it isn't needed.** Mitigated by taking the residual shortfall after other relief and showing that assumption to the operator.
- **Scope creep on the explainer.** It explains. It never decides. Expanding its role would weaken the core contribution.
- **Overclaiming.** Any claim of novelty or documented failure needs a citation, or it is removed.

---

# 10. Possible Extensions (Stretch Goals, Not Core Scope)

- **Automate the field operator's task**, with human confirmation, once the recommendation layer performs well.
- **A pluggable forecasting layer** as an input for S(t), without hard-coupling to the scheduler.
- **Interconnected zones and network structure**: reason across zones with shared shortfall limits (this brings topology back in).
- **Cross-day equity analysis**: if the project later needs it, study how cuts spread over many days, with a clearly justified definition.
- **Reinforcement-learning policy** as an extra comparison point against the optimization-based solvers.
- **Operator-interview validation** of the field constraints, when access is possible.

"""Build mild / moderate / crisis shortfall ratios from the Zenodo files.

Usage (from repo root):
  pip install -e ".[data]"
  python scripts/build_scenario_tiers.py
  python scripts/build_scenario_tiers.py --year-from 2019        # recent-years version
"""
import argparse
import json
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

from loadshed.sim.zenodo import shortfall_ratios, tier_thresholds

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--unmet", default="data/raw/zenodo_electricity_MW/peak_unmet_MW.csv")
ap.add_argument("--met", default="data/raw/zenodo_electricity_MW/corrected_peak_met_MW.csv")
ap.add_argument("--out", default="data/processed/scenarios/tiers.json")
ap.add_argument("--year-from", type=int, default=None)
ap.add_argument("--year-to", type=int, default=None)
ap.add_argument("--max-ratio", type=float, default=0.5)
ap.add_argument("--percentiles", type=float, nargs=3, default=[50, 90, 99],
                metavar=("MILD", "MODERATE", "CRISIS"))
a = ap.parse_args()

res = shortfall_ratios(a.unmet, a.met, year_from=a.year_from, year_to=a.year_to,
                       max_ratio=a.max_ratio)
pct = dict(zip(("mild", "moderate", "crisis"), a.percentiles))
thr = tier_thresholds(res.ratios, pct)

print(f"state-days with data: {res.n_state_days}")
print(f"state-days with unmet > 0: {res.n_positive}  ({100 * res.n_positive / max(1, res.n_state_days):.1f}%)")
print(f"dropped above max_ratio={a.max_ratio}: {res.n_dropped_over_cap}")
print("\nratio percentiles (non-zero days):")
for q in (10, 25, 50, 75, 90, 95, 99, 99.9):
    print(f"  P{q:<5} {res.ratios.quantile(q / 100):.4f}")
print("\nstate-days by state (top 10):")
print(res.ratios.groupby(level="State").agg(["count", "median", "max"]).sort_values("count", ascending=False).head(10).to_string())
print("\nTIERS:", {k: round(v, 4) for k, v in thr.items()})

out = Path(a.out)
out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
out.write_text(json.dumps({
    "built_on": date.today().isoformat(), "unmet_file": a.unmet, "met_file": a.met,
    "percentiles": pct, "thresholds": thr, "n_observations": int(len(res.ratios)),
    "n_dropped_over_cap": res.n_dropped_over_cap, **res.settings}, indent=2))
print("wrote", out)
