================================================
FILE: src/loadshed/ladder.py
================================================
"""The relaxation ladder. The rungs are cumulative and always tried in this order:

  rung 0  all rules hold                                         -> PLAN           (executable)
  rung 1  relax MAXIMUM DOWNTIME (soft rule), report by how much -> PLAN           (executable)
  rung 2  cut CRITICAL feeders, but only as a PROPOSAL           -> NEEDS_APPROVAL (not executable)
          listing exactly which (feeder, slot) pairs the operator must approve
  rung 3  ESCALATE: the shortfall cannot be covered within the rules. Nothing is cut automatically
          beyond what is allowed; we report the best coverage reachable and the uncovered kW per slot
          -> ESCALATE

The tool NEVER cuts a Critical feeder without approval, and it never hides a relaxation: every rung used
is listed with a magnitude. Each "no plan at this rung" is labelled PROVEN (an exact search or a necessary
check proved it) or NOT FOUND (a heuristic ran out of time), so the operator knows how far to trust it.

Operator flow:  result = solve_ladder(problem)
                if result.status == "NEEDS_APPROVAL":  show result.needs_approval; the operator decides
                    approved -> problem2 = with_approvals(problem, pairs); result2 = solve_ladder(problem2)
                    declined -> solve_ladder(problem, allow_critical_proposals=False)   (goes to ESCALATE)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from time import perf_counter

from .metrics import compute_metrics, required_relief
from .model import Problem, Schedule, Tier
from .solvers.bnb import solve_bnb
from .solvers.hybrid import solve_hybrid
from .solvers.minconflicts import solve_min_conflicts
from .solvers.patterns import enumerate_patterns
from .verify import verify

PLAN, NEEDS_APPROVAL, ESCALATE = "PLAN", "NEEDS_APPROVAL", "ESCALATE"
PROVEN, NOT_FOUND, FOUND = "proven impossible", "not found in time", "plan found"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Relaxation:
    rung: int
    rule: str            # MAX_DOWNTIME or CRITICAL_CUT
    magnitude: float     # slots over the limit / kW-slots of Critical load proposed to cut
    detail: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Attempt:
    rung: int
    label: str
    solver: str
    outcome: str         # FOUND, PROVEN, NOT_FOUND
    seconds: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LadderResult:
    rung: int
    status: str                                        # PLAN, NEEDS_APPROVAL, ESCALATE
    schedule: Schedule | None
    objective: float | None
    relaxations: tuple[Relaxation, ...]
    needs_approval: tuple[tuple[str, int], ...]        # (feeder, slot) pairs the operator must approve
    coverage_fraction: float | None                    # rung 3 only: share of the shortfall we can cover
    uncovered_kw: tuple[float, ...] | None             # rung 3 only: required relief we cannot provide, per slot
    attempts: tuple[Attempt, ...]
    messages: tuple[str, ...]

    @property
    def executable(self) -> bool:
        return self.status == PLAN

    @property
    def proven(self) -> bool:
        """True if every 'no plan at a lower rung' claim was proven, not just a heuristic giving up."""
        return all(a.outcome != NOT_FOUND for a in self.attempts)


def with_approvals(problem: Problem, pairs) -> Problem:
    """A copy of the problem in which the operator has approved these Critical (feeder, slot) cuts."""
    return replace(problem, approvals=problem.approvals | frozenset(pairs))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- one attempt
def _attempt(problem: Problem, relaxed: bool, seconds: float, solver: str, exact_max: int, seed: int,
             warm_start: Schedule | None = None):
    """Returns (schedule | None, objective | None, outcome, solver_name, elapsed).

    solver="auto": the hybrid (local search, then exact search started from its plan) up to `exact_max` feeders,
    local search above that. solver="hybrid" / "bnb" / "ls" force one choice."""
    t0 = perf_counter()
    n = len(problem.feeders)
    if solver == "hybrid" or (solver == "auto" and n <= exact_max):
        r = solve_hybrid(problem, time_limit_s=seconds, seed=seed, warm_start=warm_start,
                         relax_downtime_if_infeasible=False, force_relaxed=relaxed)
        if r.schedule is not None:
            return r.schedule, r.objective, FOUND, "hybrid", perf_counter() - t0
        return (None, None, PROVEN if r.status == "INFEASIBLE" else NOT_FOUND, "hybrid", perf_counter() - t0)
    if solver == "bnb":
        r = solve_bnb(problem, time_limit_s=seconds, relax_downtime_if_infeasible=False, force_relaxed=relaxed,
                      warm_start=warm_start)
        if r.schedule is not None:
            return r.schedule, r.objective, FOUND, "bnb", perf_counter() - t0
        if r.status == "INFEASIBLE":
            return None, None, PROVEN, "bnb", perf_counter() - t0
    r2 = solve_min_conflicts(problem, time_limit_s=seconds, seed=seed, relax_downtime_if_infeasible=False,
                             force_relaxed=relaxed, warm_start=warm_start)
    if r2.schedule is not None:
        return r2.schedule, r2.objective, FOUND, "min_conflicts", perf_counter() - t0
    return (None, None, PROVEN if r2.status == "INFEASIBLE" else NOT_FOUND, "min_conflicts",
            perf_counter() - t0)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the ladder
def solve_ladder(problem: Problem, *, allow_critical_proposals: bool = True, time_limit_s: float = 60.0,
                 solver: str = "auto", exact_max_feeders: int = 12, seed: int = 0,
                 warm_start: Schedule | None = None) -> LadderResult:
    per = max(0.5, time_limit_s / 12)
    attempts: list[Attempt] = []

    def run(prob: Problem, relaxed: bool, rung: int, label: str):
        sched, obj, outcome, name, el = _attempt(prob, relaxed, per, solver, exact_max_feeders, seed, warm_start)
        attempts.append(Attempt(rung, label, name, outcome, round(el, 3)))
        return sched, obj

    # ---- rung 0
    sched, obj = run(problem, False, 0, "all rules")
    if sched is not None:
        return _finish(PLAN, 0, problem, sched, obj, attempts, (), ())

    # ---- rung 1
    sched, obj = run(problem, True, 1, "max downtime relaxed")
    if sched is not None:
        return _finish(PLAN, 1, problem, sched, obj, attempts, _downtime_relaxations(problem, sched), ())

    # ---- rung 2: a PROPOSAL that needs the operator's approval
    has_critical = any(f.tier == Tier.CRITICAL for f in problem.feeders)
    if allow_critical_proposals and has_critical:
        H = problem.policy.horizon_slots
        every = frozenset((f.id, t) for f in problem.feeders if f.tier == Tier.CRITICAL for t in range(H))
        p2 = replace(problem, approvals=problem.approvals | every)
        sched, obj = run(p2, True, 2, "critical cuts proposed + max downtime relaxed")
        if sched is not None:
            pending = tuple(sorted((f.id, t) for f in problem.feeders if f.tier == Tier.CRITICAL
                                   for t in range(H) if sched.cut[f.id][t] == 1
                                   and (f.id, t) not in problem.approvals and (f.id, t) not in problem.forced_cut))
            rel = _downtime_relaxations(p2, sched) + _critical_relaxations(problem, pending)
            return _finish(NEEDS_APPROVAL, 2, p2, sched, obj, attempts, rel, pending)

    # ---- rung 3: ESCALATE with the best coverage reachable by allowed actions only
    return _escalate(problem, attempts, per, solver, exact_max_feeders, seed, allow_critical_proposals and has_critical)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- rung 3
def _escalate(problem: Problem, attempts: list[Attempt], per: float, solver: str, exact_max: int, seed: int,
              critical_was_tried: bool) -> LadderResult:
    pol, H = problem.policy, problem.policy.horizon_slots
    need = [s * (1 + pol.safety_margin) for s in problem.shortfall_kw]

    # optimistic coverage from the per-slot best case of every feeder (an upper bound on what is possible)
    sums = [0.0] * H
    for f in problem.feeders:
        pat = enumerate_patterns(problem, f, strict=False)
        if len(pat) == 0:
            sums = [0.0] * H
            break
        mx = pat.net.max(axis=0)
        sums = [sums[t] + float(mx[t]) for t in range(H)]
    ratios = [sums[t] / need[t] for t in range(H) if need[t] > 1e-9]
    a_hi = max(0.0, min([1.0] + ratios))

    def scaled(a: float) -> Problem:
        return replace(problem, shortfall_kw=tuple(a * s for s in problem.shortfall_kw))

    def try_cover(a: float):
        sched, _, outcome, name, el = _attempt(scaled(a), True, per, solver, exact_max, seed)
        attempts.append(Attempt(3, f"best effort: cover {a:.0%} of the shortfall", name, outcome, round(el, 3)))
        return sched

    best_a, best_sched = 0.0, None
    s_hi = try_cover(a_hi) if a_hi > 0 else None
    if s_hi is not None:
        best_a, best_sched = a_hi, s_hi
    elif a_hi > 0:
        lo, hi = 0.0, a_hi
        for _ in range(7):
            mid = (lo + hi) / 2
            s = try_cover(mid)
            if s is not None:
                lo, best_a, best_sched = mid, mid, s
            else:
                hi = mid
    if best_sched is None:
        best_sched = _zero_plan(problem)
        if best_sched is not None:
            best_a = 0.0

    uncovered = None
    if best_sched is not None:
        req = required_relief(problem, best_sched)
        relief = [sum(f.load_kw[t] for f in problem.feeders if best_sched.cut[f.id][t] == 1) for t in range(H)]
        uncovered = tuple(round(max(0.0, req[t] - relief[t]), 1) for t in range(H))
    msgs = _escalate_messages(problem, best_a, uncovered, critical_was_tried)
    return LadderResult(3, ESCALATE, best_sched, None, (), (), best_a if best_sched is not None else None,
                        uncovered, tuple(attempts), tuple(msgs))


def _zero_plan(problem: Problem) -> Schedule | None:
    """A plan for 'no shortfall': only what the rules and the operator force. None if even that is impossible."""
    r = _attempt(replace(problem, shortfall_kw=(0.0,) * problem.policy.horizon_slots), True, 1.0, "auto", 12, 0)
    return r[0]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- reporting
def _downtime_relaxations(problem: Problem, sched: Schedule) -> tuple[Relaxation, ...]:
    soft = verify(problem, sched).soft
    if not soft:
        return ()
    total = sum(v.magnitude for v in soft)
    detail = "; ".join(f"{v.feeder} off {int(v.magnitude) + problem.policy.max_downtime_slots} slots in a row "
                       f"(limit {problem.policy.max_downtime_slots}, +{int(v.magnitude)})" for v in soft)
    return (Relaxation(1, "MAX_DOWNTIME", float(total), detail),)


def _critical_relaxations(problem: Problem, pending) -> tuple[Relaxation, ...]:
    if not pending:
        return ()
    load = {f.id: f.load_kw for f in problem.feeders}
    kw = sum(load[fid][t] for fid, t in pending)
    feeders = sorted({fid for fid, _ in pending})
    return (Relaxation(2, "CRITICAL_CUT", float(kw),
                       f"approval needed to cut Critical feeder(s) {', '.join(feeders)} "
                       f"in {len(pending)} feeder-slot(s)"),)


def _finish(status: str, rung: int, problem: Problem, sched: Schedule, obj: float | None,
            attempts: list[Attempt], relaxations, pending) -> LadderResult:
    v = verify(problem, sched)
    assert v.ok, "the ladder must never return a plan the verifier rejects"
    msgs = []
    if rung == 0:
        msgs.append("RUNG 0: all rules hold. The plan is ready for the operator.")
    if rung >= 1:
        msgs.append("RUNG 1: no plan satisfies every rule, so MAXIMUM DOWNTIME was relaxed.")
        for r in relaxations:
            if r.rule == "MAX_DOWNTIME":
                msgs.append(f"   {r.detail}")
    if rung == 2:
        msgs.append("RUNG 2: the shortfall cannot be covered without Critical feeders. THIS PLAN IS A PROPOSAL AND "
                    "IS NOT EXECUTABLE until the operator approves each Critical cut listed below.")
        for fid, t in pending:
            msgs.append(f"   approve: cut {fid} in slot {t}")
        msgs.append("   If the operator declines, re-run with allow_critical_proposals=False (goes to ESCALATE).")
    if obj is None:
        obj = compute_metrics(problem, sched).total_harm
    return LadderResult(rung, status, sched, float(obj), tuple(relaxations), tuple(pending), None, None,
                        tuple(attempts), tuple(msgs))


def _escalate_messages(problem: Problem, coverage: float, uncovered, critical_was_tried: bool) -> list[str]:
    msgs = ["ESCALATE: the shortfall cannot be covered within the rules and the actions currently allowed."]
    if critical_was_tried:
        msgs.append("   Even proposing every Critical feeder for approval did not give a feasible plan.")
    else:
        msgs.append("   Critical feeders were not offered for cutting.")
    if uncovered is None:
        msgs.append("   The rules conflict even with no shortfall. A human must decide.")
        return msgs
    msgs.append(f"   Best effort covers about {coverage:.0%} of the shortfall without cutting any Critical feeder.")
    worst = max(range(len(uncovered)), key=lambda t: uncovered[t])
    msgs.append(f"   Largest uncovered relief: {uncovered[worst]:.0f} kW in slot {worst}. "
                f"Total uncovered: {sum(uncovered):.0f} kW-slots.")
    msgs.append("   Nothing beyond the best-effort partial plan is done automatically. The human decides what to do about the rest.")
    return msgs

FILE: src/loadshed/loop.py
================================================
"""Rolling-horizon replanning loop (a simulation of one shedding episode).

Every cycle:
  1. build a Problem for the next 16 slots from the CURRENT world: the history ledger (what the feeders
     actually did), the shortfall the operator currently states, estimated loads, operator overrides and approvals;
  2. solve it through the relaxation ladder (warm-started from last cycle's plan);
  3. if the ladder asks for approval of Critical cuts, ask the operator (a callback);
  4. COMMIT only the first slot, send the commands, and see what ACTUALLY happens
     (a breaker may fail to trip; real loads differ from the estimates);
  5. update the ledger from what happened, not from what was planned; advance one slot; repeat.

Why this matters: the fairness-free rules that depend on time (minimum cut/restore durations, switching
budgets, maximum downtime) only mean something if the ledger is carried from cycle to cycle.

Optional meter feedback (load_feedback): after each slot every feeder's measured load is compared with the estimate and a
per-feeder multiplier is smoothed toward the ratio, so persistent estimate errors are learned instead of insured against.

Assumptions (placeholders, see docs): a failed command still consumes one switching operation; agricultural
promised-hours windows are recomputed from the current horizon each cycle; load error is Gaussian
(a per-feeder bias plus per-slot noise); a shortfall change is known to the planner only from the slot it happens.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import random
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace
from time import perf_counter
from typing import Callable

from .ladder import ESCALATE, NEEDS_APPROVAL, LadderResult, solve_ladder, with_approvals
from .model import LONG_AGO, Feeder, FeederHistory, Problem, Schedule, Tier
from .policy import Policy
from .sim.grid import Grid, _promises, feeder_loads
from .sim.scenarios import Scenario


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- scripted events
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ShortfallChange:
    slot: int
    peak_ratio: float            # the operator now states a different shortfall ratio from this slot on


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Override:
    start: int                   # first episode slot (inclusive)
    end: int                     # last episode slot (exclusive)
    feeder_id: str
    action: str                  # "cut" or "keep"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ActuationFailure:
    slot: int
    feeder_id: str               # the command to this feeder at this slot fails (the breaker does not move)


def approve_all(result: LadderResult, problem: Problem, k: int):
    return frozenset(result.needs_approval)


def decline_all(result: LadderResult, problem: Problem, k: int):
    return None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EpisodeConfig:
    grid: Grid
    policy: Policy
    scenario: Scenario                                   # peak ratio + shape; len(shape) = episode length in slots
    start_slot: int = 68                                 # slot of day at episode slot 0 (68 = 17:00)
    shift_offset0: int = 0
    events: tuple = ()
    failure_prob: float = 0.0                            # random chance that any switching command fails
    load_error: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 0.0)         # (sd of per-feeder bias, sd of per-slot noise), as fractions
    time_limit_s: float = 6.0                            # per replan
    solver: str = "auto"
    exact_max_feeders: int = 12
    seed: int = 0
    warm_start: bool = True
    operator: Callable = decline_all
    load_feedback: tuple[float, float] | None = None   # (smoothing alpha, meter noise sd as a fraction); None = no meter feedback


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StepLog:
    slot: int
    rung: int
    status: str
    quiet: bool                      # nothing in the world changed since the previous cycle
    plan_revision: float | None      # share of overlapping (feeder, slot) entries the new plan changed
    switches: int
    failed: int
    shortfall_kw: float
    net_relief_kw: float
    unserved_kw: float
    solve_s: float
    approvals_requested: int
    approvals_granted: int
    surprises: int = 0               # feeders whose committed action differs from what the previous cycle's plan predicted


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EpisodeMetrics:
    total_harm: float            # harm actually suffered: cut harm + switch cost (no overshoot term)
    cut_harm: float
    switch_cost: float
    unserved_kw_slots: float     # shortfall NOT covered by real relief, summed over slots
    overshoot_kw_slots: float    # real relief beyond the shortfall
    shed_kwh: float
    n_switches: int
    failed_commands: int
    replans: int
    rung_counts: dict
    escalations: int
    approvals_requested: int
    approvals_granted: int
    quiet_cycles: int
    plan_revision_rate_quiet: float | None
    short_cycles: int            # on-off-on or off-on-off with the middle state <= 4 slots (ALSO counts legitimate rotation)
    commit_surprises: int        # committed actions the previous plan had not predicted, summed over cycles
    commit_surprise_rate_quiet: float | None   # share of feeders surprised per QUIET cycle (nothing changed in the world)
    unplanned_reversals: int     # an unpredicted switch that undoes a switch made at most 4 slots earlier
    cut_slots_mean: float
    cut_slots_max: int
    longest_outage_slots: int
    critical_cut_slots: int
    mean_solve_s: float
    max_solve_s: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EpisodeResult:
    executed: dict                           # feeder id -> tuple of actual states (1 = cut) over the episode
    steps: tuple
    metrics: EpisodeMetrics
    shortfall_kw: tuple                      # the real shortfall per slot
    approved: frozenset                      # (feeder, absolute slot) Critical cuts the operator approved
    overrides: tuple = field(default=())

    def executed_schedule(self) -> Schedule:
        return Schedule({fid: tuple(r) for fid, r in self.executed.items()})


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the loop
def run_episode(cfg: EpisodeConfig) -> EpisodeResult:
    pol, grid = cfg.policy, cfg.grid
    H, c = pol.horizon_slots, pol.commit_slots
    E = len(cfg.scenario.shape)
    specs = grid.specs
    ids = [s.id for s in specs]
    spd = 24 * 60 // pol.slot_minutes                                  # slots per day
    rng = random.Random(cfg.seed)

    long_pol = replace(pol, horizon_slots=E + H)
    est = {s.id: feeder_loads(s, long_pol, cfg.start_slot) for s in specs}          # estimated loads, E+H slots
    demand = [sum(est[i][g] for i in ids) for g in range(E + H)]
    bias = {i: (rng.gauss(0.0, cfg.load_error[0]) if cfg.load_error[0] > 0 else 0.0) for i in ids}
    corr = {i: 1.0 for i in ids}                         # meter feedback: learned multiplier on each feeder's load estimate

    changes = sorted((e for e in cfg.events if isinstance(e, ShortfallChange)), key=lambda e: e.slot)
    overrides = tuple(e for e in cfg.events if isinstance(e, Override))
    scripted_fail = {(e.slot, e.feeder_id) for e in cfg.events if isinstance(e, ActuationFailure)}
    event_slots = ({e.slot for e in changes} | {e.start for e in overrides} | {e.end for e in overrides}
                   | {s for s, _ in scripted_fail})

    def ratio_at(g: int) -> float:
        r = cfg.scenario.peak_ratio
        for e in changes:
            if e.slot <= g:
                r = e.peak_ratio
        return r

    def shortfall(g: int, ratio: float) -> float:
        shape = cfg.scenario.shape[g] if g < E else 0.0
        return round(ratio * shape * demand[g], 1)

    # ---- the ledger: what the feeders ACTUALLY did
    cut = {i: 0 for i in ids}
    run = {i: LONG_AGO for i in ids}
    sw = {i: 0 for i in ids}
    executed = {i: [] for i in ids}
    approved: set = set()
    steps: list[StepLog] = []
    shortfalls: list[float] = []
    prev_plan = None
    prev_k = None
    prev_failed = 0
    cut_harm = switch_cost = unserved = overshoot = shed = 0.0
    n_sw = failed_total = escalations = req_total = grant_total = 0
    rung_counts: dict = {}
    last_sw_slot = {i: None for i in ids}
    last_sw_dir = {i: None for i in ids}
    unplanned_rev = 0
    k = 0
    while k < E:
        # ---------- 1. the problem for this cycle
        feeders = tuple(
            Feeder(s.id, s.tier, s.ftype, s.consumers, tuple(x * corr[s.id] for x in est[s.id][k:k + H]),
                   _promises(s, pol, cfg.start_slot + k)) for s in specs)
        S = tuple(shortfall(g, ratio_at(k)) for g in range(k, k + H))
        forced_cut, forced_keep = set(), set()
        for o in overrides:
            for g in range(max(o.start, k), min(o.end, k + H)):
                (forced_cut if o.action == "cut" else forced_keep).add((o.feeder_id, g - k))
        problem = Problem(
            policy=pol, feeders=feeders, shortfall_kw=S,
            history={i: FeederHistory(bool(cut[i]), run[i], sw[i]) for i in ids},
            shift_offset=(cfg.shift_offset0 + k) % pol.shift_slots,
            forced_cut=frozenset(forced_cut), forced_keep=frozenset(forced_keep),
            approvals=frozenset((f, g - k) for f, g in approved if k <= g < k + H),
            start_slot=cfg.start_slot + k)

        warm = None
        if cfg.warm_start and prev_plan is not None:
            shift = k - prev_k
            warm = Schedule({i: tuple(prev_plan[i][shift:]) + (prev_plan[i][-1],) * shift for i in ids})

        # ---------- 2. solve through the ladder; 3. ask the operator about Critical proposals
        t0 = perf_counter()
        kw = dict(time_limit_s=cfg.time_limit_s, solver=cfg.solver, exact_max_feeders=cfg.exact_max_feeders,
                  seed=cfg.seed + k, warm_start=warm)
        res = solve_ladder(problem, **kw)
        requested = granted = 0
        if res.status == NEEDS_APPROVAL:
            requested = len(res.needs_approval)
            ok = cfg.operator(res, problem, k)
            if ok:
                granted = len(ok)
                approved |= {(f, k + t) for f, t in ok}
                problem = with_approvals(problem, ok)
                res = solve_ladder(problem, **kw)
            if res.status == NEEDS_APPROVAL or not ok:           # declined, or only part of what was needed
                res = solve_ladder(problem, allow_critical_proposals=False, **kw)
        solve_s = perf_counter() - t0
        rung_counts[res.rung] = rung_counts.get(res.rung, 0) + 1
        req_total += requested
        grant_total += granted
        if res.status == ESCALATE:
            escalations += 1

        # ---------- plan stability: how much of the overlap with last cycle's plan did we change?
        plan = {i: tuple(res.schedule.cut[i]) for i in ids} if res.schedule is not None else None
        revision = None
        if plan is not None and prev_plan is not None:
            shift = k - prev_k
            cells = changed = 0
            for i in ids:
                for t in range(H - shift):
                    cells += 1
                    changed += prev_plan[i][t + shift] != plan[i][t]
            revision = changed / cells if cells else None
        surprises = 0
        if plan is not None and prev_plan is not None and k - prev_k < H:
            off = k - prev_k
            surprises = sum(1 for i in ids if prev_plan[i][off] != plan[i][0])
        quiet = (prev_k is not None and not any(prev_k < e <= k for e in event_slots) and prev_failed == 0
                 and (cfg.shift_offset0 + k) % pol.shift_slots != 0 and requested == 0)

        # ---------- 4. commit the first `c` slots (stop early if something goes wrong)
        failed_this_cycle = 0
        done = 0
        for j in range(min(c, E - k)):
            g = k + j
            if (cfg.shift_offset0 + g) % pol.shift_slots == 0:
                sw = {i: 0 for i in ids}                           # a new shift: switching counters reset
            want = {i: (plan[i][j] if plan is not None else cut[i]) for i in ids}
            switches = failed = 0
            relief = surge = cut_h = 0.0
            was_cut = dict(cut)
            before_run = dict(run)
            for i in ids:
                if want[i] != cut[i]:
                    sw[i] += 1                                      # an attempt always costs one operation
                    switches += 1
                    if (g, i) in scripted_fail or (cfg.failure_prob > 0 and rng.random() < cfg.failure_prob):
                        failed += 1
                        run[i] += 1                                  # the breaker did not move: same state continues
                    else:
                        cut[i], run[i] = want[i], 1
                else:
                    run[i] += 1
                executed[i].append(cut[i])
            for i in ids:                                            # unplanned reversals: a surprise that undoes a recent switch
                if cut[i] != was_cut[i]:
                    predicted = (j == 0 and prev_plan is not None and k - prev_k < H and prev_plan[i][k - prev_k] == cut[i])
                    if (last_sw_slot[i] is not None and g - last_sw_slot[i] <= 4 and last_sw_dir[i] != cut[i]
                            and not predicted):
                        unplanned_rev += 1
                    last_sw_slot[i], last_sw_dir[i] = g, cut[i]
            tod = pol.time_of_day_weights[((cfg.start_slot + g) * pol.slot_minutes // 60) % 24]
            for s in specs:
                i = s.id
                true = est[i][g] * (1.0 + bias[i] + (rng.gauss(0.0, cfg.load_error[1]) if cfg.load_error[1] > 0 else 0.0))
                if cfg.load_feedback is not None and est[i][g] > 0:          # the meter reading corrects the next plans
                    alpha, msd = cfg.load_feedback
                    meas = true * (1.0 + (rng.gauss(0.0, msd) if msd > 0 else 0.0))
                    corr[i] = min(3.0, max(0.3, (1 - alpha) * corr[i] + alpha * meas / est[i][g]))
                if cut[i]:
                    relief += true
                    cut_h += pol.tier_weights[s.tier] * tod * s.consumers * (1 + pol.harm_beta * (run[i] - 1))
                if was_cut[i] and not cut[i]:                        # restored this slot: surge
                    surge += true * pol.surge_fraction(before_run[i])
            S_real = shortfall(g, ratio_at(g))
            net = relief - surge
            shortfalls.append(S_real)
            unserved += max(0.0, S_real - net)
            overshoot += max(0.0, net - S_real)
            shed += relief * pol.slot_minutes / 60
            cut_harm += cut_h
            switch_cost += pol.switch_mu * switches
            n_sw += switches
            failed_total += failed
            failed_this_cycle += failed
            steps.append(StepLog(g, res.rung, res.status, quiet and j == 0, revision if j == 0 else None,
                                 switches, failed, S_real, round(net, 1), round(max(0.0, S_real - net), 1),
                                 solve_s if j == 0 else 0.0, requested if j == 0 else 0, granted if j == 0 else 0,
                                 surprises if j == 0 else 0))
            done += 1
            if failed or (g + 1) in event_slots:             # something changed: replan now, not at the next cadence point
                break
        if plan is not None:
            prev_plan, prev_k, prev_failed = plan, k, failed_this_cycle
        else:
            prev_plan, prev_k, prev_failed = None, None, 0
        k += max(1, done)

    # ---------- summary
    rows = {i: tuple(r) for i, r in executed.items()}
    cut_counts = [sum(r) for r in rows.values()]
    longest = short = 0
    for r in rows.values():
        runs, cur, val = [], 0, None
        for x in r:
            if x == val:
                cur += 1
            else:
                if val is not None:
                    runs.append((val, cur))
                val, cur = x, 1
        runs.append((val, cur))
        longest = max([longest] + [n for v, n in runs if v == 1])
        short += sum(1 for m in range(1, len(runs) - 1) if runs[m][1] <= 4)
    crit = {s.id for s in specs if s.tier == Tier.CRITICAL}
    quiet_steps = [s for s in steps if s.quiet and s.plan_revision is not None]
    solves = [s.solve_s for s in steps if s.solve_s > 0]
    metrics = EpisodeMetrics(
        total_harm=cut_harm + switch_cost, cut_harm=cut_harm, switch_cost=switch_cost,
        unserved_kw_slots=unserved, overshoot_kw_slots=overshoot, shed_kwh=shed, n_switches=n_sw,
        failed_commands=failed_total, replans=sum(rung_counts.values()), rung_counts=dict(sorted(rung_counts.items())),
        escalations=escalations, approvals_requested=req_total, approvals_granted=grant_total,
        quiet_cycles=len(quiet_steps),
        plan_revision_rate_quiet=(sum(s.plan_revision for s in quiet_steps) / len(quiet_steps)) if quiet_steps else None,
        short_cycles=short, commit_surprises=sum(x.surprises for x in steps),
        commit_surprise_rate_quiet=(sum(x.surprises for x in quiet_steps) / (len(quiet_steps) * len(ids))) if quiet_steps else None,
        unplanned_reversals=unplanned_rev, cut_slots_mean=sum(cut_counts) / max(1, len(cut_counts)),
        cut_slots_max=max(cut_counts, default=0), longest_outage_slots=longest,
        critical_cut_slots=sum(sum(rows[i]) for i in crit),
        mean_solve_s=sum(solves) / len(solves) if solves else 0.0, max_solve_s=max(solves, default=0.0))
    return EpisodeResult(rows, tuple(steps), metrics, tuple(shortfalls), frozenset(approved), overrides)



================================================
FILE: src/loadshed/metrics.py

"""Objective and reporting numbers. Every solver and the CP-SAT oracle must use THIS objective.

harm = sum over cut (feeder, slot):  tier_weight * time_of_day_weight * consumers * (1 + beta*(r-1))
     + overshoot_lambda * sum over slots of (relief - required)
     + switch_mu * number of breaker operations
r = number of consecutive slots the feeder has been cut, counting history and this slot.

No fairness claim: cut-slot spread is reported as plain numbers only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from .model import Problem, Schedule, Tier


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Metrics:
    total_harm: float
    cut_harm: float
    overshoot_penalty: float
    switch_penalty: float
    shed_kwh: float
    overshoot_kw: float            # sum over slots of relief beyond the requirement
    relief_deficit_kw: float       # sum over slots of requirement not met (0 for a valid plan)
    n_switches: int
    cut_slots_mean: float          # mean cut slots per feeder (all feeders)
    cut_slots_max: int
    longest_outage_slots: int
    critical_cut_slots: int


def required_relief(problem: Problem, schedule: Schedule) -> list[float]:
    """S(t)*(1+margin) + restoration surge, per slot. Same definition the verifier enforces."""
    pol = problem.policy
    need = [problem.shortfall_kw[t] * (1 + pol.safety_margin) for t in range(pol.horizon_slots)]
    for f in problem.feeders:
        h = problem.hist(f.id)
        prev, run = (1 if h.currently_cut else 0), h.run_slots
        for t, cur in enumerate(schedule.cut[f.id]):
            if cur != prev:
                if prev == 1:
                    need[t] += f.load_kw[t] * pol.surge_fraction(run)
                prev, run = cur, 1
            else:
                run += 1
    return need


def compute_metrics(problem: Problem, schedule: Schedule) -> Metrics:
    pol = problem.policy
    H = pol.horizon_slots
    cut_harm = 0.0
    n_switches = 0
    cut_counts, longest, crit_slots = [], 0, 0

    for f in problem.feeders:
        h = problem.hist(f.id)
        w = pol.tier_weights[f.tier]
        prev, run = (1 if h.currently_cut else 0), h.run_slots
        n_cut = 0
        for t, cur in enumerate(schedule.cut[f.id]):
            if cur != prev:
                n_switches += 1
                prev, run = cur, 1
            else:
                run += 1
            if cur == 1:
                n_cut += 1
                cut_harm += w * pol.time_of_day_weights[problem.hour_of(t)] * f.consumers * (1 + pol.harm_beta * (run - 1))
                longest = max(longest, run)
                crit_slots += f.tier == Tier.CRITICAL
        cut_counts.append(n_cut)

    need = required_relief(problem, schedule)
    relief = [sum(f.load_kw[t] for f in problem.feeders if schedule.cut[f.id][t] == 1) for t in range(H)]
    over = sum(max(0.0, relief[t] - need[t]) for t in range(H))
    deficit = sum(max(0.0, need[t] - relief[t]) for t in range(H))
    slot_h = pol.slot_minutes / 60
    over_pen, sw_pen = pol.overshoot_lambda * over, pol.switch_mu * n_switches
    return Metrics(
        total_harm=cut_harm + over_pen + sw_pen, cut_harm=cut_harm, overshoot_penalty=over_pen,
        switch_penalty=sw_pen, shed_kwh=sum(relief) * slot_h, overshoot_kw=over,
        relief_deficit_kw=deficit, n_switches=n_switches,
        cut_slots_mean=sum(cut_counts) / max(1, len(cut_counts)), cut_slots_max=max(cut_counts, default=0),
        longest_outage_slots=longest, critical_cut_slots=int(crit_slots))

"""Core data types. No solver logic lives here."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .policy import Policy

LONG_AGO = 10**6  # "has been in this state for a very long time"


class Tier(str, Enum):
    FLEXIBLE = "F"   # shed first
    NORMAL = "N"
    CRITICAL = "C"   # shed last, only with operator approval


class FeederType(str, Enum):
    URBAN = "urban"
    RURAL = "rural"
    AGRICULTURAL = "agricultural"
    INDUSTRIAL = "industrial"
    MIXED = "mixed"   # carries a critical consumer; tag it with its highest tier


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PromisedWindow:
    """Feeder must be ON for at least `min_on_slots` slots within plan slots [start, end).
    The caller (simulator) already subtracts any hours delivered before slot 0."""
    start: int
    end: int
    min_on_slots: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Feeder:
    id: str
    tier: Tier
    ftype: FeederType
    consumers: int
    load_kw: tuple[float, ...]            # estimated load L_f(t), one value per slot
    promises: tuple[PromisedWindow, ...] = ()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FeederHistory:
    """What happened to this feeder before slot 0 (the downtime ledger entry)."""
    currently_cut: bool = False
    run_slots: int = LONG_AGO             # slots spent in the current state, up to now
    switches_this_shift: int = 0          # breaker operations so far in the current shift


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Problem:
    """One planning instance: everything the solver and the verifier are given."""
    policy: "Policy"
    feeders: tuple[Feeder, ...]
    shortfall_kw: tuple[float, ...]       # S(t), one value per slot
    history: dict[str, FeederHistory] = field(default_factory=dict)
    shift_offset: int = 0                 # slots already elapsed in the current shift
    forced_cut: frozenset[tuple[str, int]] = frozenset()    # operator: cut this feeder in this slot
    forced_keep: frozenset[tuple[str, int]] = frozenset()   # operator: keep this feeder ON
    approvals: frozenset[tuple[str, int]] = frozenset()     # operator approves a Critical cut
    start_slot: int = 0                   # slot-of-day at plan slot 0 (used for time-of-day harm)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        H = self.policy.horizon_slots
        ids = [f.id for f in self.feeders]
        if len(set(ids)) != len(ids):
            raise ValueError("duplicate feeder ids")
        if len(self.shortfall_kw) != H:
            raise ValueError(f"shortfall_kw needs {H} values")
        if any(s < 0 for s in self.shortfall_kw):
            raise ValueError("shortfall must be >= 0")
        if not 0 <= self.shift_offset < self.policy.shift_slots:
            raise ValueError("shift_offset must be in [0, shift_slots)")
        for f in self.feeders:
            if len(f.load_kw) != H or any(x < 0 for x in f.load_kw):
                raise ValueError(f"{f.id}: load_kw needs {H} non-negative values")
            if f.consumers < 0:
                raise ValueError(f"{f.id}: consumers must be >= 0")
            for w in f.promises:
                if not (0 <= w.start < w.end <= H) or w.min_on_slots > w.end - w.start:
                    raise ValueError(f"{f.id}: bad promised window {w}")
        known = set(ids)
        for name in ("forced_cut", "forced_keep", "approvals"):
            for fid, t in getattr(self, name):
                if fid not in known or not 0 <= t < H:
                    raise ValueError(f"{name}: bad entry {(fid, t)}")
        if self.forced_cut & self.forced_keep:
            raise ValueError("a feeder-slot cannot be both forced cut and forced keep")
        for fid in self.history:
            if fid not in known:
                raise ValueError(f"history for unknown feeder {fid}")

    def hour_of(self, t: int) -> int:
        """Clock hour (0-23) of plan slot t."""
        return ((self.start_slot + t) * self.policy.slot_minutes // 60) % 24

    def hist(self, feeder_id: str) -> FeederHistory:
        return self.history.get(feeder_id, FeederHistory())


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Schedule:
    """cut[feeder_id][t] = 1 if the feeder is cut in slot t, else 0."""
    cut: dict[str, tuple[int, ...]]

    def committed(self, k: int) -> dict[str, tuple[int, ...]]:
        """The part we actually act on (first k slots); the rest is tentative."""
        return {fid: row[:k] for fid, row in self.cut.items()}



================================================
FILE: src/loadshed/policy.py
================================================
"""Policy = every tunable number, loaded from YAML and validated."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import yaml

from .model import Tier


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Policy:
    slot_minutes: int
    horizon_slots: int
    commit_slots: int
    shift_slots: int
    tier_weights: dict[Tier, float]
    min_cut_slots: int
    min_restore_slots: int
    max_downtime_slots: int          # soft limit
    feeder_switch_budget: int
    system_switch_budget: int
    safety_margin: float
    surge_base: float
    surge_per_slot: float
    surge_max: float
    harm_beta: float
    overshoot_lambda: float
    switch_mu: float
    time_of_day_weights: tuple[float, ...]

    def surge_fraction(self, outage_slots: int) -> float:
        """Extra load, as a fraction of normal load, in the slot right after a restore."""
        return min(self.surge_max, self.surge_base + self.surge_per_slot * outage_slots)

    # ---------- loading ----------
    @classmethod
    def from_yaml(cls, path: str | Path) -> "Policy":
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return cls.from_dict(yaml.safe_load(fh))

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: dict[str, Any]) -> "Policy":
        t, s, ti, li = d["time"], d["shift"], d["tiers"], d["limits"]
        ma, su, ha = d["margins"], d["surge"], d["harm"]
        p = cls(
            slot_minutes=int(t["slot_minutes"]),
            horizon_slots=int(t["horizon_slots"]),
            commit_slots=int(t["commit_slots"]),
            shift_slots=int(s["shift_slots"]),
            tier_weights={
                Tier.FLEXIBLE: float(ti["flexible"]["weight"]),
                Tier.NORMAL: float(ti["normal"]["weight"]),
                Tier.CRITICAL: float(ti["critical"]["weight"]),
            },
            min_cut_slots=int(li["min_cut_slots"]),
            min_restore_slots=int(li["min_restore_slots"]),
            max_downtime_slots=int(li["max_downtime_slots"]),
            feeder_switch_budget=int(li["feeder_switch_budget"]),
            system_switch_budget=int(li["system_switch_budget"]),
            safety_margin=float(ma["safety_margin"]),
            surge_base=float(su["base"]),
            surge_per_slot=float(su["per_slot"]),
            surge_max=float(su["max"]),
            harm_beta=float(ha["beta"]),
            overshoot_lambda=float(ha["overshoot_lambda"]),
            switch_mu=float(ha["switch_mu"]),
            time_of_day_weights=tuple(float(x) for x in ha["time_of_day_weights"]),
        )
        p._validate()
        return p

    def _validate(self) -> None:
        def need(cond: bool, msg: str) -> None:
            if not cond:
                raise ValueError(f"policy: {msg}")

        need(self.slot_minutes > 0 and self.horizon_slots > 0, "slot_minutes and horizon_slots must be > 0")
        need(1 <= self.commit_slots <= self.horizon_slots, "commit_slots must be in [1, horizon_slots]")
        need(self.shift_slots > 0, "shift_slots must be > 0")
        w = self.tier_weights
        need(0 < w[Tier.FLEXIBLE] < w[Tier.NORMAL] < w[Tier.CRITICAL],
             "weights must satisfy 0 < flexible < normal < critical (critical is shed last)")
        need(self.min_cut_slots >= 1 and self.min_restore_slots >= 1, "min cut/restore slots must be >= 1")
        need(self.max_downtime_slots >= self.min_cut_slots, "max_downtime_slots must be >= min_cut_slots")
        need(self.feeder_switch_budget >= 0 and self.system_switch_budget >= 0, "switch budgets must be >= 0")
        need(self.safety_margin >= 0, "safety_margin must be >= 0")
        need(0 <= self.surge_base <= self.surge_max and self.surge_per_slot >= 0, "bad surge settings")
        need(len(self.time_of_day_weights) == 24, "time_of_day_weights needs 24 values")



================================================
FILE: src/loadshed/verify.py
================================================
"""Independent verifier.

Rules of this file:
  * It imports only the data types and the policy. Never a solver.
  * Plain loops, no clever tricks, so a human can audit it line by line.
  * It rebuilds everything from the Problem (including each feeder's history)
    and the Schedule. It trusts nothing the solver says about its own output.

Max downtime is soft and counts only runs the PLAN extends (a run already over the limit in history
and restored at once is not the plan's fault).

Result has three lists:
  hard   - the plan breaks a hard rule. Do not show it to the operator as valid.
  soft   - the plan breaks a soft rule (max downtime). Reported with a magnitude.
  waived - a rule was broken at a slot the OPERATOR forced. The operator's order
           wins, so this does not block the plan, but it is logged.
Relief (the shortfall rule) can never be waived: physics does not take orders.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from .model import FeederHistory, Problem, Schedule, Tier

TOL = 1e-6

# rule names
MALFORMED = "MALFORMED"
RELIEF = "RELIEF"
MIN_CUT = "MIN_CUT"
MIN_RESTORE = "MIN_RESTORE"
FEEDER_SWITCH_BUDGET = "FEEDER_SWITCH_BUDGET"
SYSTEM_SWITCH_BUDGET = "SYSTEM_SWITCH_BUDGET"
FORCED_CUT = "FORCED_CUT"
FORCED_KEEP = "FORCED_KEEP"
PROMISED_SUPPLY = "PROMISED_SUPPLY"
CRITICAL_UNAPPROVED = "CRITICAL_UNAPPROVED"
MAX_DOWNTIME = "MAX_DOWNTIME"   # soft


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Violation:
    rule: str
    feeder: str | None
    slot: int | None
    magnitude: float
    detail: str


@dataclass
class VerifyResult:
    hard: list[Violation] = field(default_factory=list)
    soft: list[Violation] = field(default_factory=list)
    waived: list[Violation] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def ok(self) -> bool:
        return not self.hard

    def rules(self, kind: str = "hard") -> set[str]:
        return {v.rule for v in getattr(self, kind)}


def verify(problem: Problem, schedule: Schedule) -> VerifyResult:
    res = VerifyResult()
    if not _check_shape(problem, schedule, res):
        return res

    H = problem.policy.horizon_slots
    switch_events: list[list[str]] = [[] for _ in range(H)]    # feeders that switch in slot t
    restores: list[list[tuple[str, int]]] = [[] for _ in range(H)]  # (feeder, outage length) restored in slot t

    for f in problem.feeders:
        _check_feeder_timeline(problem, f.id, schedule.cut[f.id], res, switch_events, restores)

    _check_system_switches(problem, res, switch_events)
    _check_relief(problem, schedule, res, restores)
    _check_overrides_and_critical(problem, schedule, res)
    _check_promises(problem, schedule, res)
    return res


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def _forced(problem: Problem, fid: str, t: int) -> bool:
    return (fid, t) in problem.forced_cut or (fid, t) in problem.forced_keep


def _flag(problem: Problem, res: VerifyResult, rule: str, fid: str, t: int,
          magnitude: float, detail: str) -> None:
    """Record a violation; if the operator forced this feeder-slot, it is waived."""
    v = Violation(rule, fid, t, magnitude, detail)
    (res.waived if _forced(problem, fid, t) else res.hard).append(v)


def _check_shape(problem: Problem, schedule: Schedule, res: VerifyResult) -> bool:
    H = problem.policy.horizon_slots
    want = {f.id for f in problem.feeders}
    have = set(schedule.cut)
    for fid in sorted(want - have):
        res.hard.append(Violation(MALFORMED, fid, None, 1, "feeder missing from schedule"))
    for fid in sorted(have - want):
        res.hard.append(Violation(MALFORMED, fid, None, 1, "unknown feeder in schedule"))
    for fid in sorted(want & have):
        row = schedule.cut[fid]
        if len(row) != H:
            res.hard.append(Violation(MALFORMED, fid, None, 1, f"needs {H} slots, got {len(row)}"))
        elif any(x not in (0, 1) for x in row):
            res.hard.append(Violation(MALFORMED, fid, None, 1, "values must be 0 or 1"))
    return not res.hard


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- per-feeder timeline
def _check_feeder_timeline(problem: Problem, fid: str, row: tuple[int, ...], res: VerifyResult,
                           switch_events: list[list[str]],
                           restores: list[list[tuple[str, int]]]) -> None:
    """Walk one feeder through time, starting from its history.

    Checks: min cut, min restore, per-feeder switch budget, max downtime (soft).
    Also records switch events and restores for the system-wide checks.
    """
    pol = problem.policy
    h: FeederHistory = problem.hist(fid)
    prev = 1 if h.currently_cut else 0
    run = h.run_slots              # slots spent in `prev` so far (includes history)
    switches = h.switches_this_shift
    plan_cut_in_run = False        # did the plan itself cut this feeder in the current run?

    for t, cur in enumerate(row):
        if (problem.shift_offset + t) % pol.shift_slots == 0:
            switches = 0           # a new shift starts at this slot

        if cur != prev:            # state change between slot t-1 and slot t
            if prev == 1:          # a cut run ends here (feeder restored)
                if run < pol.min_cut_slots:
                    _flag(problem, res, MIN_CUT, fid, t, pol.min_cut_slots - run,
                          f"restored after {run} slots, minimum cut is {pol.min_cut_slots}")
                if plan_cut_in_run:
                    _soft_downtime(res, pol.max_downtime_slots, fid, t, run)
                restores[t].append((fid, run))
            else:                  # an ON run ends here (feeder cut again)
                if run < pol.min_restore_slots:
                    _flag(problem, res, MIN_RESTORE, fid, t, pol.min_restore_slots - run,
                          f"cut again after {run} slots on, minimum restore is {pol.min_restore_slots}")
            switches += 1
            switch_events[t].append(fid)
            if switches > pol.feeder_switch_budget:
                _flag(problem, res, FEEDER_SWITCH_BUDGET, fid, t, switches - pol.feeder_switch_budget,
                      f"{switches} operations this shift, budget {pol.feeder_switch_budget}")
            prev, run = cur, 1
            plan_cut_in_run = False
        else:
            run += 1
        if cur == 1:
            plan_cut_in_run = True

    if prev == 1 and plan_cut_in_run:   # cut run still going at the end of the horizon
        _soft_downtime(res, pol.max_downtime_slots, fid, len(row) - 1, run)


def _soft_downtime(res: VerifyResult, limit: int, fid: str, t: int, run: int) -> None:
    if run > limit:
        res.soft.append(Violation(MAX_DOWNTIME, fid, t, run - limit,
                                  f"off {run} slots in a row, limit {limit}"))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- system-wide checks
def _check_system_switches(problem: Problem, res: VerifyResult,
                           switch_events: list[list[str]]) -> None:
    pol = problem.policy
    total = sum(problem.hist(f.id).switches_this_shift for f in problem.feeders)
    for t, fids in enumerate(switch_events):
        if (problem.shift_offset + t) % pol.shift_slots == 0:
            total = 0
        for fid in fids:
            total += 1
            if total > pol.system_switch_budget:
                _flag(problem, res, SYSTEM_SWITCH_BUDGET, fid, t, total - pol.system_switch_budget,
                      f"{total} operations system-wide this shift, budget {pol.system_switch_budget}")


def _check_relief(problem: Problem, schedule: Schedule, res: VerifyResult,
                  restores: list[list[tuple[str, int]]]) -> None:
    """Relief in each slot must cover S(t) with margin, plus the surge from feeders restored in that slot."""
    pol = problem.policy
    load = {f.id: f.load_kw for f in problem.feeders}
    for t in range(pol.horizon_slots):
        relief = sum(load[f.id][t] for f in problem.feeders if schedule.cut[f.id][t] == 1)
        surge = sum(load[fid][t] * pol.surge_fraction(run) for fid, run in restores[t])
        need = problem.shortfall_kw[t] * (1 + pol.safety_margin) + surge
        if relief < need - TOL:
            res.hard.append(Violation(RELIEF, None, t, need - relief,
                                      f"relief {relief:.1f} kW, need {need:.1f} kW (incl. surge {surge:.1f})"))


def _check_overrides_and_critical(problem: Problem, schedule: Schedule, res: VerifyResult) -> None:
    for fid, t in sorted(problem.forced_cut):
        if schedule.cut[fid][t] != 1:
            res.hard.append(Violation(FORCED_CUT, fid, t, 1, "operator forced a cut, schedule keeps it on"))
    for fid, t in sorted(problem.forced_keep):
        if schedule.cut[fid][t] != 0:
            res.hard.append(Violation(FORCED_KEEP, fid, t, 1, "operator forced keep-on, schedule cuts it"))
    for f in problem.feeders:
        if f.tier != Tier.CRITICAL:
            continue
        for t, x in enumerate(schedule.cut[f.id]):
            # an operator-forced cut counts as approval: the human already decided
            if x == 1 and (f.id, t) not in problem.approvals and (f.id, t) not in problem.forced_cut:
                res.hard.append(Violation(CRITICAL_UNAPPROVED, f.id, t, 1,
                                          "critical feeder cut without operator approval"))


def _check_promises(problem: Problem, schedule: Schedule, res: VerifyResult) -> None:
    for f in problem.feeders:
        row = schedule.cut[f.id]
        for w in f.promises:
            on = sum(1 for t in range(w.start, w.end) if row[t] == 0)
            if on < w.min_on_slots:
                res.hard.append(Violation(PROMISED_SUPPLY, f.id, w.start, w.min_on_slots - on,
                                          f"on {on} slots in [{w.start},{w.end}), promised {w.min_on_slots}"))

================================================
FILE: src/loadshed/sim/grid.py
================================================
"""Synthetic grid: feeders with tiers, types, sizes and daily load shapes.

EVERYTHING numeric in this file is a documented PLACEHOLDER (shares, sizes, profiles),
to be calibrated later from tariff orders / discom documents (see docs/field-constraints.md).
Same seed -> same grid.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from dataclasses import dataclass

from ..model import Feeder, FeederHistory, FeederType, Problem, PromisedWindow, Tier
from ..policy import Policy
from .scenarios import Scenario

# ---- placeholder assumptions --------------------------------------------------------
TIER_SHARE = {Tier.CRITICAL: 0.05, Tier.FLEXIBLE: 0.15}      # the rest is NORMAL

TYPE_MIX = {                                                  # feeder type given tier
    Tier.CRITICAL: ((FeederType.MIXED, 0.7), (FeederType.RURAL, 0.3)),     # hospital area / water pumping
    Tier.FLEXIBLE: ((FeederType.INDUSTRIAL, 1.0),),
    Tier.NORMAL:   ((FeederType.URBAN, 0.45), (FeederType.RURAL, 0.35), (FeederType.AGRICULTURAL, 0.20)),
}

# consumers (low, high) and reference kW per consumer
SIZE = {
    FeederType.URBAN:        (800, 3000, 1.0),
    FeederType.RURAL:        (300, 1500, 0.7),
    FeederType.AGRICULTURAL: (100, 600, 4.0),
    FeederType.INDUSTRIAL:   (5, 60, 90.0),
    FeederType.MIXED:        (1000, 4000, 1.0),
}

# load multiplier by hour of day (0..23). Reference kW x multiplier = load in that hour.
_URBAN = [0.45] * 6 + [0.60, 0.65, 0.65] + [0.65] * 8 + [0.85] + [1.0] * 4 + [0.8, 0.6]
_RURAL = [0.30] * 6 + [0.45] * 3 + [0.40] * 8 + [0.70] + [1.0] * 4 + [0.7, 0.45]
_INDUS = [0.55] * 6 + [0.80] * 2 + [0.95] * 10 + [0.85] * 4 + [0.70, 0.60]
PROFILE = {FeederType.URBAN: _URBAN, FeederType.MIXED: _URBAN, FeederType.RURAL: _RURAL,
           FeederType.INDUSTRIAL: _INDUS}
assert all(len(p) == 24 for p in PROFILE.values())

# agricultural supply blocks (start hour, end hour), wrapping past midnight allowed
AG_BLOCKS = ((6, 14), (14, 22), (22, 6))
AG_PROMISE_SHARE = 0.75          # at least 75% of the block slots inside the horizon must be ON
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FeederSpec:
    id: str
    tier: Tier
    ftype: FeederType
    consumers: int
    base_kw: float
    ag_block: tuple[int, int] | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Grid:
    specs: tuple[FeederSpec, ...]
    seed: int

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.specs)


def slot_of_day(hour: int, minute: int = 0, slot_minutes: int = 15) -> int:
    return (hour * 60 + minute) // slot_minutes


def _in_block(hour: int, block: tuple[int, int]) -> bool:
    s, e = block
    return s <= hour < e if s < e else (hour >= s or hour < e)


def _tier_counts(n: int) -> dict[Tier, int]:
    if n < 3:
        raise ValueError("need at least 3 feeders (one per tier)")
    crit = max(1, round(n * TIER_SHARE[Tier.CRITICAL]))
    flex = max(1, round(n * TIER_SHARE[Tier.FLEXIBLE]))
    return {Tier.CRITICAL: crit, Tier.FLEXIBLE: flex, Tier.NORMAL: n - crit - flex}


def make_grid(n_feeders: int, seed: int = 0) -> Grid:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    specs: list[FeederSpec] = []
    for tier, count in _tier_counts(n_feeders).items():
        types, weights = zip(*TYPE_MIX[tier])
        for _ in range(count):
            ft = rng.choices(types, weights)[0]
            lo, hi, kwpc = SIZE[ft]
            consumers = rng.randint(lo, hi)
            base = round(consumers * kwpc * rng.lognormvariate(0.0, 0.15), 1)
            block = rng.choice(AG_BLOCKS) if ft == FeederType.AGRICULTURAL else None
            specs.append(FeederSpec("", tier, ft, consumers, base, block))
    rng.shuffle(specs)                                   # no tier ordering bias
    width = len(str(n_feeders - 1))
    specs = [FeederSpec(f"f{i:0{width}d}", s.tier, s.ftype, s.consumers, s.base_kw, s.ag_block)
             for i, s in enumerate(specs)]
    return Grid(tuple(specs), seed)


def _hour(policy: Policy, start_slot: int, t: int) -> int:
    return ((start_slot + t) * policy.slot_minutes // 60) % 24


def feeder_loads(spec: FeederSpec, policy: Policy, start_slot: int) -> tuple[float, ...]:
    """Estimated load L_f(t) for each slot of the horizon (kW)."""
    out = []
    for t in range(policy.horizon_slots):
        h = _hour(policy, start_slot, t)
        if spec.ftype == FeederType.AGRICULTURAL:
            out.append(spec.base_kw if _in_block(h, spec.ag_block) else 0.0)
        else:
            out.append(round(spec.base_kw * PROFILE[spec.ftype][h], 1))
    return tuple(out)


def _promises(spec: FeederSpec, policy: Policy, start_slot: int) -> tuple[PromisedWindow, ...]:
    if spec.ag_block is None:
        return ()
    inside = [t for t in range(policy.horizon_slots)
              if _in_block(_hour(policy, start_slot, t), spec.ag_block)]
    if not inside:
        return ()
    start, end = inside[0], inside[-1] + 1
    return (PromisedWindow(start, end, math.ceil(AG_PROMISE_SHARE * (end - start))),)


def build_problem(grid: Grid, policy: Policy, scenario: Scenario, start_slot: int, *,
                  episode_offset: int = 0,
                  history: dict[str, FeederHistory] | None = None,
                  shift_offset: int = 0,
                  forced_cut: frozenset = frozenset(),
                  forced_keep: frozenset = frozenset(),
                  approvals: frozenset = frozenset()) -> Problem:
    """One planning instance for the horizon starting at `start_slot` of the day.

    S(t) = scenario.peak_ratio * scenario.shape[episode_offset + t] * total_demand(t).
    Past the end of the episode the shortfall is 0.
    """
    H = policy.horizon_slots
    feeders = tuple(
        Feeder(s.id, s.tier, s.ftype, s.consumers, feeder_loads(s, policy, start_slot),
               _promises(s, policy, start_slot)) for s in grid.specs)
    demand = [sum(f.load_kw[t] for f in feeders) for t in range(H)]
    shape = [scenario.shape[episode_offset + t] if episode_offset + t < len(scenario.shape) else 0.0
             for t in range(H)]
    shortfall = tuple(round(scenario.peak_ratio * shape[t] * demand[t], 1) for t in range(H))
    return Problem(policy=policy, feeders=feeders, shortfall_kw=shortfall,
                   history=history or {}, shift_offset=shift_offset,
                   forced_cut=forced_cut, forced_keep=forced_keep, approvals=approvals)



================================================
FILE: src/loadshed/sim/scenarios.py
================================================
"""Shortfall scenarios.

A scenario = a peak shortfall RATIO (share of demand that cannot be served)
           + a SHAPE over the episode (0..1 per slot).
S(t) = peak_ratio * shape[t] * demand(t).

The ratio comes from the Zenodo data (see zenodo.py). The shape is a documented
synthetic trapezoid, because the Zenodo data is daily and cannot give intra-day shape.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Scenario:
    name: str
    peak_ratio: float
    shape: tuple[float, ...]       # one value in [0, 1] per slot of the episode


def trapezoid(n_slots: int, ramp_slots: int = 4) -> tuple[float, ...]:
    """Ramp up, hold at 1.0, ramp down. Ramps shrink if the episode is short."""
    if n_slots < 1:
        raise ValueError("n_slots must be >= 1")
    ramp = max(0, min(ramp_slots, n_slots // 2))
    out = []
    for t in range(n_slots):
        up = (t + 1) / (ramp + 1) if ramp else 1.0
        down = (n_slots - t) / (ramp + 1) if ramp else 1.0
        out.append(min(1.0, up, down))
    return tuple(out)


def make_scenario(name: str, peak_ratio: float, episode_slots: int = 32,
                  ramp_slots: int = 4) -> Scenario:
    if not 0 <= peak_ratio < 1:
        raise ValueError("peak_ratio must be in [0, 1)")
    return Scenario(name, peak_ratio, trapezoid(episode_slots, ramp_slots))


def load_tiers(path: str | Path, episode_slots: int = 32,
               ramp_slots: int = 4) -> dict[str, Scenario]:
    """Read data/processed/scenarios/tiers.json (written by scripts/build_scenario_tiers.py)."""
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        blob = json.load(fh)
    return {name: make_scenario(name, float(r), episode_slots, ramp_slots)
            for name, r in blob["thresholds"].items()}



================================================
FILE: src/loadshed/sim/zenodo.py
================================================
"""Turn the Zenodo state demand files into shortfall-ratio statistics.

ratio = unmet / (met + unmet), on days where unmet > 0.
This needs pandas (pip install -e ".[data]"). The model and verifier do not.

Choices (all written into tiers.json so they can be cited):
  * corrected peak-met file is used for 'met'; raw peak-unmet for 'unmet' (no corrected version exists)
  * non-state columns (Total, AMNSIL, DVC) are excluded by default
  * duplicate dates: keep the first row
  * ratios above max_ratio are dropped as suspect outliers and counted
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

NON_STATE = ("Total", "AMNSIL", "Damodar Valley Corporation")


def read_wide(path: str | Path) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Read a Zenodo wide file: one row per date, one column per state."""
    df = pd.read_csv(path)
    date_col = next((c for c in df.columns if str(c).strip().lower() in ("date", "datetime")),
                    df.columns[0])
    df = df.rename(columns={date_col: "Date"})
    df = df.drop(columns=[c for c in df.columns if str(c).strip().lower() == "occurrence"])
    df["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Date"], errors="coerce")
    df = df.dropna(subset=["Date"]).drop_duplicates("Date", keep="first")
    df = df.set_index("Date").sort_index()
    return df.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")


@dataclass
class RatioResult:
    ratios: pd.Series                       # index: (Date, State); value: unmet/(met+unmet)
    n_state_days: int = 0                   # state-days with both values present
    n_positive: int = 0                     # of those, unmet > 0
    n_dropped_over_cap: int = 0
    settings: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


def shortfall_ratios(unmet_csv: str | Path, met_csv: str | Path, *,
                     exclude: tuple[str, ...] = NON_STATE,
                     year_from: int | None = None, year_to: int | None = None,
                     states: list[str] | None = None,
                     max_ratio: float = 0.5) -> RatioResult:
    unmet, met = read_wide(unmet_csv), read_wide(met_csv)
    cols = [c for c in unmet.columns if c in met.columns and c not in exclude]
    if states is not None:
        cols = [c for c in cols if c in states]
    idx = unmet.index.intersection(met.index)
    if year_from is not None:
        idx = idx[idx.year >= year_from]
    if year_to is not None:
        idx = idx[idx.year <= year_to]
    u, m = unmet.loc[idx, cols], met.loc[idx, cols]

    both = u.notna() & m.notna() & ((u + m) > 0)
    pos = both & (u > 0)
    ratio = (u / (u + m)).where(pos)
    long = ratio.stack().dropna()           # only unmet>0 state-days remain (explicit: pandas versions differ)
    long.index.names = ["Date", "State"]
    over = long > max_ratio
    return RatioResult(
        ratios=long[~over], n_state_days=int(both.to_numpy().sum()),
        n_positive=int(pos.to_numpy().sum()), n_dropped_over_cap=int(over.sum()),
        settings={"year_from": year_from, "year_to": year_to, "max_ratio": max_ratio,
                  "excluded_columns": list(exclude), "n_state_columns": len(cols)})


def tier_thresholds(ratios: pd.Series, percentiles: dict[str, float]) -> dict[str, float]:
    """e.g. {"mild": 50, "moderate": 90, "crisis": 99} -> ratio at each percentile."""
    if len(ratios) == 0:
        raise ValueError("no positive-unmet observations to take percentiles from")
    out = {name: float(np.percentile(ratios.to_numpy(), q)) for name, q in percentiles.items()}
    vals = list(out.values())
    if vals != sorted(vals):
        raise ValueError("percentiles must be increasing")
    return out
