"""The rolling-horizon loop. The strongest check: what was ACTUALLY executed, cycle after cycle, must pass the
verifier as ONE plan over the whole episode (so minimum durations, switching budgets and shift resets held
across replans, not just inside each plan)."""
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

pytest.importorskip("ortools")

from loadshed import Feeder, Policy, Problem, Tier, verify
from loadshed.loop import (ActuationFailure, EpisodeConfig, Override, ShortfallChange, approve_all, decline_all,
                           run_episode)
from loadshed.sim import make_grid, make_scenario
from loadshed.sim.grid import feeder_loads

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
POL = Policy.from_yaml(ROOT / "configs" / "policy.yaml")


def cfg(n=6, ratio=0.0684, E=10, pol=POL, **kw):
    return EpisodeConfig(grid=make_grid(n, 0), policy=pol, scenario=make_scenario("t", ratio, episode_slots=E),
                         time_limit_s=2, **kw)


def whole_episode_check(c, res):
    """Verify the executed history as a single plan covering the whole episode."""
    E = len(c.scenario.shape)
    pol = replace(c.policy, horizon_slots=E)
    feeders = tuple(Feeder(s.id, s.tier, s.ftype, s.consumers, feeder_loads(s, pol, c.start_slot)) for s in c.grid.specs)
    fc = frozenset((o.feeder_id, g) for o in res.overrides if o.action == "cut" for g in range(o.start, min(o.end, E)))
    fk = frozenset((o.feeder_id, g) for o in res.overrides if o.action == "keep" for g in range(o.start, min(o.end, E)))
    prob = Problem(policy=pol, feeders=feeders, shortfall_kw=res.shortfall_kw, shift_offset=c.shift_offset0,
                   forced_cut=fc, forced_keep=fk, approvals=frozenset((f, g) for f, g in res.approved if g < E),
                   start_slot=c.start_slot)
    return verify(prob, res.executed_schedule())


def first_cut(res):
    for g in range(len(res.steps)):
        for i, row in res.executed.items():
            if row[g] == 1 and (g == 0 or row[g - 1] == 0):
                return g, i


def test_executed_history_passes_the_verifier_as_one_plan():
    c = cfg()
    res = run_episode(c)
    assert whole_episode_check(c, res).ok
    assert res.metrics.unserved_kw_slots == 0 and res.metrics.rung_counts == {0: 10}
    assert res.metrics.critical_cut_slots == 0 and len(res.steps) == 10


def test_switching_budget_resets_at_shift_boundaries_across_cycles():
    # 4-slot shifts, 2 switches per feeder per shift and a 3-slot downtime limit FORCE rotation every shift.
    # It is only solvable at rung 0 if the ledger's switch counters reset when a new shift starts.
    tight = replace(POL, shift_slots=4, feeder_switch_budget=2, system_switch_budget=8, max_downtime_slots=3)
    c = cfg(E=12, pol=tight)
    res = run_episode(c)
    assert res.metrics.rung_counts == {0: 12} and res.metrics.unserved_kw_slots == 0
    assert whole_episode_check(c, res).ok
    for a in (0, 4, 8):                                           # every shift really did switch something
        assert any(row[t] != (row[t - 1] if t else 0) for row in res.executed.values() for t in range(a, a + 4))


def test_same_seed_same_episode():
    a, b = run_episode(cfg(failure_prob=0.3, seed=7)), run_episode(cfg(failure_prob=0.3, seed=7))
    assert a.executed == b.executed and a.metrics.failed_commands == b.metrics.failed_commands


def test_a_failed_command_is_observed_counted_and_replanned_around():
    base = run_episode(cfg())
    g, f = first_cut(base)
    c = cfg(events=(ActuationFailure(g, f),))
    res = run_episode(c)
    assert res.metrics.failed_commands == 1 and res.executed[f][g] == 0       # the breaker did not move
    assert res.steps[g].failed == 1 and res.steps[g].unserved_kw > 0          # the shortfall was really not relieved
    assert res.steps[g + 1].unserved_kw == 0                                  # the very next plan compensates
    assert res.metrics.n_switches >= base.metrics.n_switches + 1              # the failed attempt used an operation


def test_operator_overrides_are_obeyed_and_the_plan_stays_valid():
    base = run_episode(cfg())
    _, f = first_cut(base)
    other = next(s.id for s in cfg().grid.specs if s.id != f and s.tier == Tier.NORMAL)
    c = cfg(events=(Override(2, 8, f, "keep"), Override(3, 6, other, "cut")))
    res = run_episode(c)
    assert all(x == 0 for x in res.executed[f][2:8]) and all(x == 1 for x in res.executed[other][3:6])
    assert whole_episode_check(c, res).ok and res.metrics.unserved_kw_slots == 0


def test_a_shortfall_change_is_picked_up_from_the_slot_it_happens():
    base = run_episode(cfg(ratio=0.05))
    c = cfg(ratio=0.05, events=(ShortfallChange(5, 0.15),))
    res = run_episode(c)
    assert res.shortfall_kw[:5] == base.shortfall_kw[:5] and res.shortfall_kw[5] > 2 * base.shortfall_kw[5]
    assert res.steps[5].unserved_kw == 0 and res.steps[5].net_relief_kw >= res.shortfall_kw[5]
    assert whole_episode_check(c, res).ok


def critical_only_config(approve):
    c0 = cfg(E=8)
    crit = {s.id for s in c0.grid.specs if s.tier == Tier.CRITICAL}
    pol = c0.policy
    est = {s.id: feeder_loads(s, replace(pol, horizon_slots=16), c0.start_slot) for s in c0.grid.specs}
    ratio = 0.5 * min(sum(est[i][g] for i in crit) / sum(e[g] for e in est.values()) for g in range(8))
    keep = tuple(Override(0, 8, s.id, "keep") for s in c0.grid.specs if s.id not in crit)
    return cfg(E=8, ratio=ratio, events=keep, operator=approve_all if approve else decline_all)


def test_critical_cuts_happen_only_after_the_operator_approves():
    yes_cfg = critical_only_config(True)
    yes = run_episode(yes_cfg)
    assert yes.metrics.critical_cut_slots > 0 and yes.metrics.approvals_granted > 0
    assert yes.metrics.unserved_kw_slots == 0 and whole_episode_check(yes_cfg, yes).ok
    no = run_episode(critical_only_config(False))
    assert no.metrics.critical_cut_slots == 0 and no.metrics.escalations > 0
    assert no.metrics.approvals_granted == 0 and no.metrics.unserved_kw_slots > 0


def test_a_bigger_safety_margin_buys_protection_against_load_error_at_a_price():
    thin = run_episode(cfg(ratio=0.25, load_error=(0.2, 0.0), seed=2, pol=replace(POL, safety_margin=0.05)))
    fat = run_episode(cfg(ratio=0.25, load_error=(0.2, 0.0), seed=2, pol=replace(POL, safety_margin=0.40)))
    assert thin.metrics.unserved_kw_slots > 0 and fat.metrics.unserved_kw_slots == 0
    assert fat.metrics.total_harm > 1.5 * thin.metrics.total_harm
    # learning each feeder's real load from its meter removes the shortfall the thin margin leaves, without a fat margin
    fb = run_episode(cfg(ratio=0.25, load_error=(0.2, 0.0), seed=2, pol=replace(POL, safety_margin=0.05), load_feedback=(0.7, 0.0)))
    assert fb.metrics.unserved_kw_slots == 0 and fb.metrics.total_harm > thin.metrics.total_harm


def test_warm_start_keeps_plans_valid_and_metrics_are_well_formed():
    c = cfg(ratio=0.2, E=8)
    for ws in (True, False):
        res = run_episode(replace(c, warm_start=ws))
        m = res.metrics
        assert whole_episode_check(replace(c, warm_start=ws), res).ok
        assert m.replans == 8 and m.total_harm == pytest.approx(m.cut_harm + m.switch_cost)
        assert m.plan_revision_rate_quiet is None or 0.0 <= m.plan_revision_rate_quiet <= 1.0
        n = len(c.grid.specs)
        quiet = [x for x in res.steps if x.quiet and x.plan_revision is not None]
        assert m.commit_surprises == sum(x.surprises for x in res.steps) and m.unplanned_reversals >= 0
        if quiet:
            assert m.commit_surprise_rate_quiet == pytest.approx(sum(x.surprises for x in quiet) / (len(quiet) * n))
            assert 0.0 <= m.commit_surprise_rate_quiet <= 1.0

import pytest

from loadshed import FeederHistory, verify
from loadshed.metrics import compute_metrics, required_relief
from tests.helpers import GOOD, policy, problem, sched


def test_hand_computed_harm():
    m = compute_metrics(problem(), GOOD)
    # N1 cut 4 slots: 5*400*(1+1.5+2+2.5)=14000 ; N2 cut 4 slots: 5*300*7=10500
    assert m.cut_harm == pytest.approx(24500)
    assert m.overshoot_kw == pytest.approx(400)            # N1 gives 400 vs 300 needed, 4 slots
    assert m.overshoot_penalty == pytest.approx(0.02 * 400)
    assert m.n_switches == 3 and m.switch_penalty == pytest.approx(3.0)
    assert m.total_harm == pytest.approx(24500 + 8 + 3)
    assert m.shed_kwh == pytest.approx((400 * 4 + 300 * 4) * 0.25)
    assert (m.cut_slots_max, m.longest_outage_slots, m.critical_cut_slots) == (4, 4, 0)
    assert m.cut_slots_mean == pytest.approx(2.0) and m.relief_deficit_kw == 0


def test_history_run_length_raises_harm():
    p = problem(history={"N1": FeederHistory(currently_cut=True, run_slots=2)})
    s = sched(N1=(1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0), N2=(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1))
    m = compute_metrics(p, s)
    # N1 slots are now the 3rd..6th consecutive cut slot: 5*400*(2+2.5+3+3.5)=22000
    assert m.cut_harm == pytest.approx(22000 + 10500)
    assert m.n_switches == 2                                # no switch at slot 0, N1 restore + N2 cut


def test_time_of_day_weight_is_used():
    pol = policy(harm={"time_of_day_weights": [2.0] + [1.0] * 23})   # hour 0 (slots 0-3) costs double
    m = compute_metrics(problem(pol=pol), GOOD)
    assert m.cut_harm == pytest.approx(2 * 14000 + 10500)


def test_required_relief_includes_surge_and_matches_verifier():
    pol = policy(surge={"base": 0.5, "per_slot": 0.0, "max": 0.5})
    p = problem(pol=pol)
    need = required_relief(p, GOOD)
    assert need[4] == pytest.approx(300 + 400 * 0.5) and need[0] == 300
    r = verify(p, GOOD)
    v = [x for x in r.hard if x.rule == "RELIEF"][0]
    assert v.magnitude == pytest.approx(need[4] - 300)
    assert compute_metrics(p, GOOD).relief_deficit_kw == pytest.approx(200)

FILE: tests/test_minconflicts.py

"""Local search is checked against the oracle (never below the optimum, usually at it), the verifier
(never invalid), the greedy baselines (never worse) and the branch-and-bound lower bound."""
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

pytest.importorskip("ortools")

from evaluation.oracle_cpsat import solve_oracle
from loadshed import Policy, Problem, verify
from loadshed.metrics import compute_metrics
from loadshed.sim import build_problem, make_grid, make_scenario, slot_of_day
from loadshed.solvers import solve_bnb, solve_greedy, solve_greedy_sticky, solve_min_conflicts
from tests.helpers import H as H8, policy as pol8, problem as prob8
from tests.test_bnb import random_tiny

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
POL = Policy.from_yaml(ROOT / "configs" / "policy.yaml")
TIERS = {"mild": 0.0296, "moderate": 0.0684, "crisis": 0.2}


def grid_problem(n, tier, seed, hour, **kw):
    return build_problem(make_grid(n, seed), POL, make_scenario(tier, TIERS[tier]), slot_of_day(hour),
                         episode_offset=8, **kw)


def test_on_random_tiny_problems_it_is_valid_never_below_optimum_and_usually_optimal():
    at_opt, feasible = 0, 0
    for seed in range(100, 125):
        p = random_tiny(seed)
        o = solve_oracle(p, time_limit_s=20, workers=1)
        r = solve_min_conflicts(p, time_limit_s=10, seed=1, max_iters=1500)
        if o.status == "INFEASIBLE":
            assert r.schedule is None and r.status in ("INFEASIBLE", "UNKNOWN")
            continue
        feasible += 1
        assert r.schedule is not None and verify(p, r.schedule).ok
        assert r.objective >= o.objective - 1e-6                      # nothing can beat the proven optimum
        at_opt += abs(r.objective - o.objective) <= 1e-6 * max(1.0, o.objective)
        assert r.mode == o.mode or abs(r.objective - o.objective) > 1e-6   # same ladder rung when optimal
    assert at_opt >= feasible - 2


@pytest.mark.parametrize("n,tier", [(10, "mild"), (10, "crisis"), (50, "moderate")])
def test_never_worse_than_the_best_valid_greedy_and_always_valid(n, tier):
    for seed in range(3):
        p = grid_problem(n, tier, seed, 17)
        best = min(compute_metrics(p, s.schedule).total_harm for s in (solve_greedy(p), solve_greedy_sticky(p))
                   if verify(p, s.schedule).ok and not verify(p, s.schedule).soft)
        r = solve_min_conflicts(p, time_limit_s=20, seed=seed, max_iters=300)
        assert verify(p, r.schedule).ok and r.objective <= best + 1e-6
        assert r.start_objective == pytest.approx(best)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("tier,seed", [("mild", 0), ("moderate", 1), ("crisis", 1)])
def test_objective_respects_the_branch_and_bound_lower_bound(tier, seed):
    p = grid_problem(10, tier, seed, 17)
    lb = solve_bnb(p, node_limit=1).lower_bound
    r = solve_min_conflicts(p, time_limit_s=20, seed=0, max_iters=800)
    assert r.objective >= lb - 1e-6


def test_improves_on_the_greedy_when_there_is_room():
    p = grid_problem(50, "moderate", 0, 17)
    r = solve_min_conflicts(p, time_limit_s=30, seed=0, max_iters=600)
    assert r.objective < 0.9 * r.start_objective and verify(p, r.schedule).ok


def test_same_seed_and_iterations_give_the_same_plan():
    p = grid_problem(10, "moderate", 0, 17)
    a = solve_min_conflicts(p, time_limit_s=30, seed=5, max_iters=400)
    b = solve_min_conflicts(p, time_limit_s=30, seed=5, max_iters=400)
    assert a.schedule == b.schedule and a.objective == b.objective


def test_operator_overrides_are_respected():
    base = grid_problem(10, "moderate", 0, 17)
    target = base.feeders[0].id
    keep = grid_problem(10, "moderate", 0, 17, forced_keep=frozenset((target, t) for t in range(POL.horizon_slots)))
    cut = grid_problem(10, "moderate", 0, 17, forced_cut=frozenset({(target, 2), (target, 3)}))
    rk = solve_min_conflicts(keep, time_limit_s=20, seed=0, max_iters=300)
    rc = solve_min_conflicts(cut, time_limit_s=20, seed=0, max_iters=300)
    assert verify(keep, rk.schedule).ok and all(x == 0 for x in rk.schedule.cut[target])
    assert verify(cut, rc.schedule).ok and rc.schedule.cut[target][2:4] == (1, 1)


def test_infeasible_without_approval_is_proven_and_with_approval_it_solves():
    pol = pol8(limits={"system_switch_budget": 10})
    feeders = prob8(pol=pol).feeders
    hard = Problem(policy=pol, feeders=feeders, shortfall_kw=(1250.0,) * H8)
    r = solve_min_conflicts(hard, time_limit_s=10, max_iters=200)
    assert r.status == "INFEASIBLE" and r.schedule is None
    ok = Problem(policy=pol, feeders=feeders, shortfall_kw=(1250.0,) * H8,
                 approvals=frozenset(("C1", t) for t in range(H8)))
    r2 = solve_min_conflicts(ok, time_limit_s=10, max_iters=500)
    assert r2.schedule is not None and verify(ok, r2.schedule).ok


def test_relaxes_max_downtime_only_when_strict_has_no_plan():
    p = prob8(pol=pol8(limits={"max_downtime_slots": 3}))
    r = solve_min_conflicts(p, time_limit_s=10, seed=0, max_iters=800)
    assert r.mode == "relaxed_downtime" and verify(p, r.schedule).rules("soft") == {"MAX_DOWNTIME"}
    easy = solve_min_conflicts(prob8(), time_limit_s=10, seed=0, max_iters=800)
    assert easy.mode == "strict" and verify(prob8(), easy.schedule).ok


def test_shared_patterns_give_the_same_plan_and_setup_is_reported_separately():
    from loadshed.solvers.patterns import build_patterns
    p = grid_problem(10, "moderate", 0, 17)
    a = solve_min_conflicts(p, time_limit_s=30, seed=3, max_iters=300)
    pats = build_patterns(p, True)
    b = solve_min_conflicts(p, time_limit_s=30, seed=3, max_iters=300, patterns=pats)
    assert a.schedule == b.schedule and a.objective == b.objective
    assert a.setup_s > 0 and b.setup_s < 0.05 and a.runtime_s >= a.setup_s

FILE: tests/test_oracle.py

"""The oracle is checked against brute force: on tiny problems, enumerate EVERY schedule,
keep those the verifier accepts, and take the minimum of metrics.total_harm.
The oracle must match that number exactly. This ties oracle == verifier + metrics."""
import itertools
from dataclasses import replace

import pytest

pytest.importorskip("ortools")

from evaluation.oracle_cpsat import solve_oracle
from loadshed import (Feeder, FeederHistory, FeederType, Policy, Problem, PromisedWindow,
                      Schedule, Tier, verify)
from loadshed.metrics import compute_metrics
from tests.helpers import BASE_POLICY, H as H8, policy as pol8, problem as prob8
from copy import deepcopy


def tiny_policy(**over):
    d = deepcopy(BASE_POLICY)
    d["time"]["horizon_slots"] = 5
    d["shift"]["shift_slots"] = 6
    d["limits"].update({"min_cut_slots": 2, "min_restore_slots": 2, "max_downtime_slots": 3,
                        "feeder_switch_budget": 2, "system_switch_budget": 3})
    d["surge"] = {"base": 0.10, "per_slot": 0.05, "max": 0.30}
    d["margins"]["safety_margin"] = 0.05
    d["harm"]["time_of_day_weights"] = [1.0, 2.0] + [1.0] * 22
    for sec, vals in over.items():
        d[sec].update(vals)
    return Policy.from_dict(d)


def tiny_problem(pol=None, shortfall=(150.0, 200.0, 200.0, 100.0, 150.0), **kw):
    pol = pol or tiny_policy()
    spec = [("A", Tier.FLEXIBLE, 100.0, 5), ("B", Tier.NORMAL, 220.0, 300), ("C", Tier.NORMAL, 180.0, 200)]
    feeders = tuple(Feeder(i, t, FeederType.URBAN, n, (kw_,) * 5) for i, t, kw_, n in spec)
    return Problem(policy=pol, feeders=feeders, shortfall_kw=shortfall, start_slot=2, **kw)


def brute_force(p, strict=True):
    ids = [f.id for f in p.feeders]
    best = None
    rows = list(itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=5))
    for combo in itertools.product(rows, repeat=len(ids)):
        s = Schedule(dict(zip(ids, combo)))
        v = verify(p, s)
        if not v.ok or (strict and v.soft):
            continue
        h = compute_metrics(p, s).total_harm
        if best is None or h < best:
            best = h
    return best


def check_against_brute_force(p):
    """Strict optimum if one exists; else relaxed-downtime optimum; else the oracle must say INFEASIBLE."""
    got = solve_oracle(p, time_limit_s=20, workers=1)
    strict = brute_force(p, strict=True)
    if strict is not None:
        assert got.status == "OPTIMAL" and got.mode == "strict"
        want = strict
    else:
        relaxed = brute_force(p, strict=False)
        if relaxed is None:
            assert got.status == "INFEASIBLE"
            return "infeasible"
        assert got.status == "OPTIMAL" and got.mode == "relaxed_downtime"
        want = relaxed
    assert verify(p, got.schedule).ok
    assert got.objective == pytest.approx(want, rel=1e-6)
    return got.mode


@pytest.mark.parametrize("hist", [
    {},
    {"B": FeederHistory(currently_cut=True, run_slots=1)},                       # must stay cut one more slot
    {"A": FeederHistory(currently_cut=False, run_slots=1, switches_this_shift=1)},  # cannot be cut yet
    {"C": FeederHistory(currently_cut=True, run_slots=2, switches_this_shift=1)},
])
def test_oracle_matches_brute_force(hist):
    check_against_brute_force(tiny_problem(history=hist, shift_offset=2))


def test_oracle_matches_brute_force_with_overrides_and_promise():
    feeders = (Feeder("A", Tier.FLEXIBLE, FeederType.URBAN, 5, (100.0,) * 5),
               Feeder("B", Tier.NORMAL, FeederType.AGRICULTURAL, 300, (220.0,) * 5, (PromisedWindow(0, 5, 3),)),
               Feeder("C", Tier.NORMAL, FeederType.URBAN, 200, (180.0,) * 5))
    p = Problem(policy=tiny_policy(), feeders=feeders, shortfall_kw=(150.0, 200.0, 200.0, 100.0, 150.0),
                start_slot=2, forced_keep=frozenset({("C", 1)}), forced_cut=frozenset({("A", 0)}))
    check_against_brute_force(p)


def test_oracle_detects_infeasible_without_critical_approval():
    pol = pol8(limits={"system_switch_budget": 10})
    feeders = prob8(pol=pol).feeders                  # non-critical 1200 kW, critical 300 kW
    p = Problem(policy=pol, feeders=feeders, shortfall_kw=(1250.0,) * H8)
    assert solve_oracle(p, time_limit_s=10).status == "INFEASIBLE"
    ok = Problem(policy=pol, feeders=feeders, shortfall_kw=(1250.0,) * H8,
                 approvals=frozenset(("C1", t) for t in range(H8)))
    r = solve_oracle(ok, time_limit_s=10)
    assert r.status == "OPTIMAL" and verify(ok, r.schedule).ok and sum(r.schedule.cut["C1"]) == H8


def test_oracle_relaxes_max_downtime_only_when_strict_is_infeasible():
    pol = pol8(limits={"max_downtime_slots": 3})
    p = prob8(pol=pol)
    r = solve_oracle(p, time_limit_s=10)
    assert r.status == "OPTIMAL" and r.mode == "relaxed_downtime"
    v = verify(p, r.schedule)
    assert v.ok and v.rules("soft") == {"MAX_DOWNTIME"}
    assert solve_oracle(p, time_limit_s=10, relax_downtime_if_infeasible=False).status == "INFEASIBLE"
    easy = solve_oracle(prob8(), time_limit_s=10)         # default 4-slot limit is feasible
    assert easy.mode == "strict" and easy.status == "OPTIMAL"


def test_hint_does_not_change_the_optimum():
    from tests.helpers import GOOD
    p = prob8()
    a = solve_oracle(p, time_limit_s=10, workers=1)
    b = solve_oracle(p, time_limit_s=10, workers=1, hint=GOOD)
    assert a.objective == pytest.approx(b.objective, rel=1e-9) and a.objective <= compute_metrics(p, GOOD).total_harm + 1e-6


@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", range(10))
def test_oracle_matches_brute_force_on_random_tiny_problems(seed):
    import random
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    pol = tiny_policy(limits={"feeder_switch_budget": rng.choice([1, 2, 3]),
                              "system_switch_budget": rng.choice([2, 3, 4, 5]),
                              "min_cut_slots": rng.choice([1, 2]), "min_restore_slots": rng.choice([1, 2, 3]),
                              "max_downtime_slots": rng.choice([2, 3, 4])},
                      shift={"shift_slots": rng.choice([3, 4, 6])})
    hist = {}
    for fid in "ABC":
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            hist[fid] = FeederHistory(currently_cut=rng.random() < 0.4, run_slots=rng.randint(1, 4),
                                      switches_this_shift=rng.randint(0, 2))
    shortfall = tuple(float(rng.choice([0, 80, 120, 150, 200])) for _ in range(5))
    forced_keep = frozenset({("C", rng.randint(0, 4))}) if rng.random() < 0.3 else frozenset()
    p = tiny_problem(pol=pol, shortfall=shortfall, history=hist, forced_keep=forced_keep,
                     shift_offset=rng.randint(0, pol.shift_slots - 1))
    check_against_brute_force(p)

FILE: tests/test_patterns.py

"""Pattern enumeration must equal 'every row the verifier accepts for this one feeder'."""
import itertools
import random
from dataclasses import replace

import numpy as np
import pytest

from loadshed import Feeder, FeederHistory, FeederType, Problem, PromisedWindow, Schedule, Tier, verify
from loadshed.metrics import compute_metrics
from loadshed.solvers.patterns import enumerate_patterns, prune_dominated
from tests.test_oracle import tiny_policy

H = 5


def one_feeder_problem(seed):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    pol = tiny_policy(limits={"feeder_switch_budget": rng.choice([1, 2, 3]), "min_cut_slots": rng.choice([1, 2]),
                              "min_restore_slots": rng.choice([1, 2, 3]), "max_downtime_slots": rng.choice([2, 3, 4])},
                      shift={"shift_slots": rng.choice([3, 4, 6])})
    pol = replace(pol, system_switch_budget=1000)                       # isolate the single-feeder rules
    tier = rng.choice([Tier.NORMAL, Tier.NORMAL, Tier.CRITICAL])
    promises = (PromisedWindow(0, H, rng.choice([2, 3])),) if rng.random() < 0.3 else ()
    f = Feeder("A", tier, FeederType.URBAN, 100, tuple(float(rng.choice([50, 120, 200])) for _ in range(H)), promises)
    hist = {"A": FeederHistory(currently_cut=rng.random() < 0.4, run_slots=rng.randint(1, 4),
                               switches_this_shift=rng.randint(0, 2))} if rng.random() < 0.7 else {}
    t = rng.randint(0, H - 1)
    fc = frozenset({("A", t)}) if rng.random() < 0.2 else frozenset()
    fk = frozenset({("A", (t + 1) % H)}) if rng.random() < 0.2 and not fc else frozenset()
    ap = frozenset(("A", u) for u in range(H)) if tier == Tier.CRITICAL and rng.random() < 0.5 else frozenset()
    return Problem(policy=pol, feeders=(f,), shortfall_kw=(0.0,) * H, history=hist, forced_cut=fc, forced_keep=fk,
                   approvals=ap, shift_offset=rng.randint(0, pol.shift_slots - 1), start_slot=2)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("strict", [True, False])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", range(25))
def test_patterns_equal_rows_the_verifier_accepts(seed, strict):
    p = one_feeder_problem(seed)
    want = set()
    for row in itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=H):
        v = verify(p, Schedule({"A": row}))
        if not (v.rules("hard") - {"RELIEF"}) and not (strict and v.soft):
            want.add(row)
    got = enumerate_patterns(p, p.feeders[0], strict)
    assert {tuple(int(x) for x in r) for r in got.rows} == want


@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", range(25))
def test_pattern_cost_and_net_match_metrics(seed):
    p = one_feeder_problem(seed)
    pat = enumerate_patterns(p, p.feeders[0], False)
    c0 = -p.policy.overshoot_lambda * sum(s * (1 + p.policy.safety_margin) for s in p.shortfall_kw)
    for i in range(len(pat)):
        if (pat.net[i] < 0).any():
            continue                      # metrics clips negative overshoot; linear cost is only exact when net >= 0
        s = Schedule({"A": tuple(int(x) for x in pat.rows[i])})
        assert compute_metrics(p, s).total_harm == pytest.approx(pat.cost[i] + c0, abs=1e-6)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", range(10))
def test_dominance_never_removes_the_cheapest_cover(seed):
    p = one_feeder_problem(seed)
    pat = enumerate_patterns(p, p.feeders[0], False)
    kept = prune_dominated(pat)
    if len(pat) == 0:                     # a feeder can have no valid pattern at all (infeasible instance)
        assert len(kept) == 0
        return
    assert 0 < len(kept) <= len(pat)
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    for _ in range(20):                    # for any per-slot requirement, the best cost is unchanged
        need = np.array([rng.choice([0, 50, 100, 200]) for _ in range(H)], float)
        def best(P):
            ok = (P.net >= need - 1e-9).all(axis=1)
            return P.cost[ok].min() if ok.any() else np.inf
        assert best(kept) == pytest.approx(best(pat))

"""The fast pattern builder must give EXACTLY the patterns of the simple reference builder (same rows, same costs,
same relief, same switch events), for every feeder, in every situation."""
import random
import time
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pytest

from loadshed import FeederHistory, Policy, Tier
from loadshed.sim import build_problem, make_grid, make_scenario, slot_of_day
from loadshed.solvers.patterns import build_patterns, clear_pattern_cache
from tests.test_patterns import one_feeder_problem

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
POL = Policy.from_yaml(ROOT / "configs" / "policy.yaml")


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def fresh_cache():
    clear_pattern_cache()
    yield
    clear_pattern_cache()


def same(a, b):
    ka = {r.tobytes(): i for i, r in enumerate(a.rows)}
    kb = {r.tobytes(): i for i, r in enumerate(b.rows)}
    if set(ka) != set(kb):
        return False
    ia, ib = [ka[k] for k in kb], [kb[k] for k in kb]
    return all(np.allclose(getattr(a, f)[ia], getattr(b, f)[ib], rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-7)
               for f in ("cost", "net", "ev", "nfev"))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("strict", [True, False])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", range(25))
def test_single_feeder_problems_with_histories_overrides_and_promises(seed, strict):
    p = one_feeder_problem(seed)
    fast, ref = build_patterns(p, strict), build_patterns(p, strict, fast=False)
    assert same(fast[0], ref[0])


def messy_problem(n, seed):
    """A grid problem with random histories, operator overrides and approvals."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    base = build_problem(make_grid(n, seed), POL, make_scenario("t", 0.07), slot_of_day(rng.choice([3, 10, 17])),
                         episode_offset=8)
    H, ids = POL.horizon_slots, [f.id for f in base.feeders]
    hist = {i: FeederHistory(rng.random() < 0.3, rng.randint(1, 15), rng.randint(0, 4)) for i in ids if rng.random() < 0.6}
    fk = frozenset((rng.choice(ids), rng.randrange(H)) for _ in range(6))
    fc = frozenset((rng.choice(ids), rng.randrange(H)) for _ in range(4)) - fk
    crit = [f.id for f in base.feeders if f.tier == Tier.CRITICAL]
    ap = frozenset((c, t) for c in crit for t in range(H) if rng.random() < 0.3)
    return replace(base, history=hist, forced_keep=fk, forced_cut=fc, approvals=ap, shift_offset=rng.randrange(POL.shift_slots))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", range(4))
def test_grids_with_random_histories_overrides_and_approvals(seed):
    p = messy_problem(30, seed)
    for strict in (True, False):
        fast, ref = build_patterns(p, strict), build_patterns(p, strict, fast=False)
        assert all(same(a, b) for a, b in zip(fast, ref))


def test_a_warm_cache_gives_the_same_answer_as_a_cold_one():
    p = messy_problem(30, 7)
    cold = build_patterns(p, True)
    warm = build_patterns(p, True)                         # now served from the cache
    assert all(same(a, b) for a, b in zip(cold, warm))
    other_loads = build_patterns(messy_problem(30, 8), True)   # a different grid reuses structure, not numbers
    ref = build_patterns(messy_problem(30, 8), True, fast=False)
    assert all(same(a, b) for a, b in zip(other_loads, ref))


def test_kept_patterns_are_non_dominated_and_pruning_removes_some():
    from loadshed.solvers.patterns import enumerate_patterns
    p = messy_problem(20, 3)
    fast = build_patterns(p, True)
    removed = 0
    for f, x in zip(p.feeders, fast):
        removed += len(enumerate_patterns(p, f, True)) - len(x)          # a feeder may legitimately have no pattern at all
        for i in range(len(x)):                                           # sorted by cost: only LATER patterns can be dominated
            dom = ((x.cost[i] <= x.cost + 1e-9) & (x.net[i] >= x.net - 1e-9).all(axis=1)
                   & (x.ev[i] <= x.ev).all(axis=1) & (x.nfev[i] <= x.nfev).all(axis=1))
            assert not (dom & (np.arange(len(x)) > i)).any()
    assert removed > 0


def test_it_is_much_faster_than_the_reference():
    p = build_problem(make_grid(60, 0), replace(POL, system_switch_budget=36), make_scenario("t", 0.07),
                      slot_of_day(17), episode_offset=8)
    t = time.perf_counter(); build_patterns(p, True, fast=False); ref_s = time.perf_counter() - t
    clear_pattern_cache()
    t = time.perf_counter(); build_patterns(p, True); fast_s = time.perf_counter() - t
    assert fast_s * 4 < ref_s, (fast_s, ref_s)

from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from loadshed import Policy, Problem, Tier
from tests.helpers import BASE_POLICY, H, feeders, policy

    p = Policy.from_yaml(ROOT / "configs" / "policy.yaml")
    assert (p.slot_minutes, p.horizon_slots, p.commit_slots) == (15, 16, 1)
    assert p.min_cut_slots == p.min_restore_slots == 2 and p.max_downtime_slots == 12
    assert p.feeder_switch_budget == 3 and p.system_switch_budget == 20
    assert p.tier_weights[Tier.CRITICAL] > p.tier_weights[Tier.NORMAL] > p.tier_weights[Tier.FLEXIBLE]

def test_critical_must_be_the_heaviest_tier():

        policy(tiers={"critical": {"weight": 2.0}})      # lower than normal (5.0)


def test_surge_fraction_is_capped():
    p = policy(surge={"base": 0.05, "per_slot": 0.1, "max": 0.3})
    assert p.surge_fraction(1) == pytest.approx(0.15) and p.surge_fraction(50) == 0.3

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        Problem(policy(), feeders(), (300.0,) * (H - 1))                       # wrong S length
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        Problem(policy(), feeders(), (300.0,) * H, forced_cut=frozenset({("N1", 0)}),
                forced_keep=frozenset({("N1", 0)}))                            # both forced
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        Problem(policy(), feeders(), (300.0,) * H, approvals=frozenset({("NOPE", 0)}))

import csv
from pathlib import Path

pytest.importorskip("ortools")

from evaluation.run_ladder_stats import FIELDS, load_rows, run_instance, summarize
from loadshed import Policy

POL = Policy.from_yaml(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "configs" / "policy.yaml")


def test_an_easy_scenario_stays_at_rung_0():

    assert (r["rung"], r["status"]) == (0, "PLAN") and r["extra_downtime_slots"] == 0 and r["harm"] > 0

"""Smoke tests so the robustness script keeps working (the real experiments take minutes)."""
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

pytest.importorskip("ortools")

from evaluation.run_robustness import (FIELDS, build_cfg, episode_row, idle_feeders, load_rows, most_cut_feeders,
                                       summarize)
from loadshed import Policy, Tier

def test_one_episode_row_has_every_field_and_sane_values():
    cfg = build_cfg(POL, 6, 0, 0.2, episode_slots=6, time_limit_s=2)
    res, row = episode_row("margin", 0.1, 0.05, 6, 0, cfg)
    assert set(FIELDS) <= set(row) and row["replans"] == 6 and row["harm"] >= 0 and row["unserved"] >= 0

def test_most_cut_and_idle_feeder_helpers():
    cfg = build_cfg(POL, 6, 0, 0.2, episode_slots=6, time_limit_s=2)
    res, _ = episode_row("override", "none", 0, 6, 0, cfg)
    cut = most_cut_feeders(res, 3)
    assert all(sum(res.executed[f]) > 0 for f in cut)
    assert [sum(res.executed[f]) for f in cut] == sorted((sum(res.executed[f]) for f in cut), reverse=True)
    crit = {s.id for s in cfg.grid.specs if s.tier == Tier.CRITICAL}
    idle = idle_feeders(res, cfg.grid, 10)
    assert all(sum(res.executed[f]) == 0 and f not in crit for f in idle)


def test_summary_handles_every_experiment(tmp_path, capsys):
    import csv

    def row(**kw):
        base = {k: 1.0 for k in FIELDS}
        base.update(experiment="margin", param1="0.2", param2="0.05", n=10, seed=0, harm=100.0, unserved=0.0,
                    plan_revision_quiet=0.01, surprise_quiet=0.0)
        base.update(kw)
        return base

    rows = [row(), row(param2="0.3", harm=150.0, seed=1),
            row(experiment="stability", param1="mild", param2="True"), row(experiment="stability", param1="mild", param2="False"),
            row(experiment="override", param1="none", param2="0"), row(experiment="override", param1="keep", param2="1", harm=300.0),
            row(experiment="failure", param1="0.0", param2="0"), row(experiment="failure", param1="0.2", param2="0", failed=2.0),
            row(experiment="feedback", param1="0.2", param2="no feedback, margin 5%"),
            row(experiment="feedback", param1="0.2", param2="feedback (alpha 0.7, exact meter), margin 5%")]
    path = tmp_path / "rob.csv"
    with open(path, "w", newline="") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=FIELDS)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    summarize(load_rows(path))
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    for name in ("margin:", "stability:", "override:", "failure:", "feedback:"):
        assert name in out
    assert "3.0x" in out                                   # the override doubled-and-more: 300 / 100

import json

import pytest

from loadshed import Policy, Schedule, Tier, verify
from loadshed.sim import (build_problem, load_tiers, make_grid, make_scenario,
                          slot_of_day, trapezoid)
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
POL = Policy.from_yaml(ROOT / "configs" / "policy.yaml")
EVENING = slot_of_day(17)


# ---------- grid
def test_grid_is_deterministic_and_seed_sensitive():
    assert make_grid(50, seed=1) == make_grid(50, seed=1)
    assert make_grid(50, seed=1) != make_grid(50, seed=2)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("n", [10, 50, 200, 500])
def test_grid_sizes_and_tiers(n):
    g = make_grid(n, seed=3)
    assert len(g) == n and len({s.id for s in g.specs}) == n
    tiers = [s.tier for s in g.specs]
    assert tiers.count(Tier.CRITICAL) >= 1 and tiers.count(Tier.FLEXIBLE) >= 1
    assert tiers.count(Tier.NORMAL) > n / 2
    assert all(s.base_kw > 0 for s in g.specs)


def test_too_small_grid_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        make_grid(2)


# ---------- scenarios
def test_trapezoid_shape():
    s = trapezoid(32, 4)
    assert len(s) == 32 and max(s) == 1.0 and 0 < s[0] < 1 and 0 < s[-1] < 1
    assert s[16] == 1.0 and all(0 <= x <= 1 for x in s)


def test_scenario_rejects_bad_ratio():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        make_scenario("x", 1.0)


# ---------- build_problem
@pytest.mark.parametrize("seed", range(5))
@pytest.mark.parametrize("start", [EVENING, slot_of_day(3), slot_of_day(10), slot_of_day(22)])
def test_built_problems_are_valid(seed, start):
    p = build_problem(make_grid(50, seed), POL, make_scenario("t", 0.08), start)
    assert len(p.shortfall_kw) == POL.horizon_slots and max(p.shortfall_kw) > 0


def test_shortfall_scales_with_ratio_and_ends_with_episode():
    g = make_grid(50, 0)
    lo = build_problem(g, POL, make_scenario("lo", 0.02), EVENING)
    hi = build_problem(g, POL, make_scenario("hi", 0.10), EVENING)
    assert all(h >= l for h, l in zip(hi.shortfall_kw, lo.shortfall_kw)) and sum(hi.shortfall_kw) > 4 * sum(lo.shortfall_kw)
    done = build_problem(g, POL, make_scenario("hi", 0.10, episode_slots=32), EVENING, episode_offset=40)
    assert set(done.shortfall_kw) == {0.0}


def test_agricultural_feeders_off_outside_block_and_promised_inside():
    g = make_grid(200, 0)
    p = build_problem(g, POL, make_scenario("t", 0.05), EVENING)
    ag = [f for f in p.feeders if f.ftype.value == "agricultural"]
    assert ag and any(f.promises for f in ag) and any(not f.promises and sum(f.load_kw) == 0 for f in ag)
    for f in ag:
        for w in f.promises:
            assert all(f.load_kw[t] > 0 for t in range(w.start, w.end))


def test_mild_shortfall_is_coverable_by_non_critical_load():
    p = build_problem(make_grid(50, 0), POL, make_scenario("mild", 0.05), EVENING)
    for t in range(POL.horizon_slots):
        sheddable = sum(f.load_kw[t] for f in p.feeders if f.tier != Tier.CRITICAL)
        assert sheddable >= p.shortfall_kw[t] * (1 + POL.safety_margin)


def test_verifier_rejects_the_do_nothing_schedule_on_a_real_problem():
    p = build_problem(make_grid(10, 0), POL, make_scenario("t", 0.08), EVENING)
    nothing = Schedule({f.id: (0,) * POL.horizon_slots for f in p.feeders})
    r = verify(p, nothing)
    assert not r.ok and r.rules("hard") <= {"RELIEF", "PROMISED_SUPPLY"} and "RELIEF" in r.rules("hard")


# ---------- tiers.json
def test_load_tiers(tmp_path):
    f = tmp_path / "tiers.json"
    f.write_text(json.dumps({"thresholds": {"mild": 0.02, "moderate": 0.06, "crisis": 0.15}}))
    t = load_tiers(f)
    assert list(t) == ["mild", "moderate", "crisis"] and t["crisis"].peak_ratio == 0.15

FILE: tests/test_verify.py

import pytest

from loadshed import FeederHistory, PromisedWindow, verify
from tests.helpers import GOOD, H, Z, policy, problem, sched


def hard(p, s):
    return verify(p, s).rules("hard")


# ---------- the happy path
def test_valid_schedule_passes():
    r = verify(problem(), GOOD)
    assert r.ok and not r.hard and not r.soft and not r.waived


# ---------- relief
def test_relief_shortfall_is_flagged_per_slot():
    r = verify(problem(), sched(N1=(1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0)))      # nothing covers slots 4-7
    slots = {v.slot for v in r.hard if v.rule == "RELIEF"}
    assert slots == {4, 5, 6, 7}


def test_safety_margin_is_applied():
    r = verify(problem(pol=policy(margins={"safety_margin": 0.10})), GOOD)   # N2: 300 < 330
    assert "RELIEF" in r.rules("hard")


def test_restoration_surge_raises_the_requirement():
    p = problem(pol=policy(surge={"base": 0.5, "per_slot": 0.0, "max": 0.5}))
    r = verify(p, GOOD)           # N1 restored in slot 4: need 300 + 400*0.5 = 500, have 300
    v = [x for x in r.hard if x.rule == "RELIEF"]
    assert [x.slot for x in v] == [4] and v[0].magnitude == pytest.approx(200.0)


# ---------- critical tier
def test_critical_cut_needs_approval():
    s = sched(N1=(1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0), C1=(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1))
    assert "CRITICAL_UNAPPROVED" in hard(problem(), s)
    approved = frozenset(("C1", t) for t in range(4, 8))
    assert verify(problem(approvals=approved), s).ok


def test_operator_forced_cut_counts_as_approval():
    s = sched(N1=(1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0), C1=(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1))
    forced = frozenset(("C1", t) for t in range(4, 8))
    assert verify(problem(forced_cut=forced), s).ok


# ---------- minimum durations (in-plan and from history)
def test_min_cut_in_plan():
    assert "MIN_CUT" in hard(problem(), sched(N1=(1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)))


def test_min_restore_in_plan():
    assert "MIN_RESTORE" in hard(problem(), sched(N1=(1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)))


def test_min_cut_uses_history():
    p = problem(history={"N1": FeederHistory(currently_cut=True, run_slots=1)})
    assert "MIN_CUT" in hard(p, sched())              # restored at slot 0 after only 1 slot cut


def test_min_restore_uses_history():
    p = problem(history={"N1": FeederHistory(currently_cut=False, run_slots=1)})
    assert "MIN_RESTORE" in hard(p, sched(N1=(1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0)))


def test_history_cut_that_is_long_enough_may_restore():
    p = problem(history={"N1": FeederHistory(currently_cut=True, run_slots=2)})
    assert "MIN_CUT" not in hard(p, sched())


# ---------- switching budgets
def test_feeder_budget_counts_history():
    p = problem(shift_offset=2, history={"N1": FeederHistory(switches_this_shift=2)})
    assert "FEEDER_SWITCH_BUDGET" in hard(p, GOOD)


def test_feeder_budget_resets_at_shift_boundary():
    s = sched(N1=(0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0))            # first switch at t=2
    hist = {"N1": FeederHistory(switches_this_shift=2)}
    # shift boundary at t=2 (offset 6): counter resets, two switches fit
    assert "FEEDER_SWITCH_BUDGET" not in hard(problem(shift_offset=6, history=hist), s)
    # boundary at t=6 (offset 2): the t=2 switch is the 3rd of the shift
    assert "FEEDER_SWITCH_BUDGET" in hard(problem(shift_offset=2, history=hist), s)


def test_system_budget_counts_history_of_all_feeders():
    p = problem(shift_offset=2, history={"F1": FeederHistory(switches_this_shift=1)})
    # GOOD has 3 switches (N1 cut, N1 restore, N2 cut) + 1 from history = 4 > 3
    assert "SYSTEM_SWITCH_BUDGET" in hard(p, GOOD)
    assert verify(problem(shift_offset=2), GOOD).ok    # without that history it fits exactly


# ---------- operator overrides
def test_forced_cut_must_be_respected():
    assert "FORCED_CUT" in hard(problem(forced_cut=frozenset({("F1", 0)})), GOOD)


def test_forced_keep_must_be_respected():
    assert "FORCED_KEEP" in hard(problem(forced_keep=frozenset({("N1", 0)})), GOOD)


def test_override_waives_duration_rule_but_not_relief():
    s = sched(N1=(1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0))             # restored after 1 slot: breaks MIN_CUT at t=1
    r = verify(problem(forced_keep=frozenset({("N1", 1)})), s)
    assert "MIN_CUT" in r.rules("waived") and "MIN_CUT" not in r.rules("hard")
    assert "RELIEF" in r.rules("hard")                  # physics is never waived


# ---------- promised supply
def test_promised_supply_hours():
    p = problem(promises={"N2": [PromisedWindow(0, 8, 5)]})
    assert "PROMISED_SUPPLY" in hard(p, GOOD)           # N2 is on only 4 of 8 slots
    assert "PROMISED_SUPPLY" not in hard(problem(promises={"N2": [PromisedWindow(0, 8, 4)]}), GOOD)


# ---------- soft rule
def test_max_downtime_is_soft_with_magnitude():
    r = verify(problem(), sched(N1=(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)))    # 5 slots, limit 4
    assert [(v.rule, v.magnitude) for v in r.soft] == [("MAX_DOWNTIME", 1)]
    assert "MAX_DOWNTIME" not in r.rules("hard")


def test_downtime_run_that_started_in_history_counts():
    p = problem(history={"N1": FeederHistory(currently_cut=True, run_slots=4)})
    r = verify(p, sched(N1=(1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)))             # 4 + 2 = 6 slots
    assert any(v.rule == "MAX_DOWNTIME" and v.magnitude == 2 for v in r.soft)


# ---------- malformed input
@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [
    {"N1": (1, 1)},                                  # wrong length
    {"N1": (2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)},                # not 0/1
])
def test_malformed_rows(bad):
    assert verify(problem(), sched(**bad)).rules("hard") == {"MALFORMED"}


def test_missing_and_unknown_feeders():
    s = sched()
    cut = dict(s.cut)
    del cut["C1"]
    cut["ZZ"] = Z
    r = verify(problem(), type(s)(cut))
    assert r.rules("hard") == {"MALFORMED"} and len(r.hard) == 2


def test_history_run_over_limit_is_not_blamed_on_the_plan():
    p = problem(history={"N1": FeederHistory(currently_cut=True, run_slots=6)})   # already over limit 4
    assert verify(p, sched()).soft == []                         # restored at once: nothing the plan did
    r = verify(p, sched(N1=(1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)))            # plan extends it by one slot
    assert [(v.rule, v.magnitude) for v in r.soft] == [("MAX_DOWNTIME", 3)]   # 7 slots vs limit 4

import pytest

pd = pytest.importorskip("pandas")

from loadshed.sim.zenodo import read_wide, shortfall_ratios, tier_thresholds


def _write(tmp_path):
    dates = ["2013-01-01", "2013-01-02", "2013-01-02", "2014-01-01", "2020-01-01"]   # one duplicate date
    unmet = pd.DataFrame({"Date": dates, "Occurrence": [0, 0, 1, 0, 0],
                          "A": [0, 10, 99, 20, 30], "B": [None, 0, 0, 5, 1000], "Total": [1, 1, 1, 1, 1]})
    met = pd.DataFrame({"Date": dates, "Occurrence": [0, 0, 1, 0, 0],
                        "A": [90, 90, 90, 80, 70], "B": [50, 50, 50, 45, 50], "Total": [9, 9, 9, 9, 9]})
    u, m = tmp_path / "unmet.csv", tmp_path / "met.csv"
    unmet.to_csv(u, index=False)
    met.to_csv(m, index=False)
    return u, m


def test_read_wide_drops_duplicates_and_occurrence(tmp_path):
    u, _ = _write(tmp_path)
    df = read_wide(u)
    assert len(df) == 4 and "Occurrence" not in df.columns and df.loc["2013-01-02", "A"] == 10


def test_ratios_exclude_non_states_zeros_and_outliers(tmp_path):
    u, m = _write(tmp_path)
    r = shortfall_ratios(u, m)
    vals = {k: round(v, 4) for k, v in r.ratios.items()}
    assert set(r.ratios.index.get_level_values("State")) == {"A", "B"}          # Total excluded
    assert len(r.ratios) == 4                      # A:10,20,30  B:5   (B:1000 -> ratio ~0.95 dropped)
    assert r.n_dropped_over_cap == 1 and r.n_positive == 5
    assert round(10 / 100, 4) in vals.values()


def test_year_filter(tmp_path):
    u, m = _write(tmp_path)
    assert len(shortfall_ratios(u, m, year_from=2014).ratios) == 3             # A:20, B:5, A:30 (B 2020 is over the cap)


def test_no_nan_in_ratios_and_thresholds_increase(tmp_path):
    u, m = _write(tmp_path)
    r = shortfall_ratios(u, m)
    assert not r.ratios.isna().any()
    t = tier_thresholds(r.ratios, {"mild": 50, "moderate": 90, "crisis": 99})
    assert t["mild"] <= t["moderate"] <= t["crisis"] and all(v == v for v in t.values())
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        tier_thresholds(r.ratios, {"a": 90, "b": 50})
